text._Subtitle: That's one of my personal favorites. You should have seen the look on your face. You'd best hurry. Next time, it might really be your friend.

text.Ardyn: Are you certain it wasn't the real thing? Wouldn't want to make a mistake.
Oh, it's just so unfair!

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn chuckles
Noct takes an elevator to an upper level and proceeds across a bridge leading to Zegnautus Keep's central elevator

text.Ardyn: Your heart's desire, so close now. Soon it will be within your grasp. I suggest you take the central elevator. It will take you to your goal.

text.Noctis: Don't look down, don't look down.

text.SYSTEM: You do not have a suitable keycard.

text.Noctis: Gotta find a way to make it move.

text.NARRATIVE: Coming to two large slightly ajar blast doors, Noctis sees a cargo area on the other side; an enormous gargantuan daemon walks by within

text.SYSTEM: Search for the keycard to operate the central elevator.

CHOICE.Ardyn: Oh, now they've found you.

text.NARRATIVE: Within the cargo area, Noctis locates the Generator Keycard at a desk

Making it back to the central elevator area, Noctis uses the Generator Keycard to restore power to the elevator; as Noctis then begins to walk back across the catwalk from the generator panel to the platform the elevator rests on, Ardyn broadcasts his voice again

text.Ardyn: The higher you climb... ... the further you fall.

text.NARRATIVE: A gargantua daemon suddenly lands on the platform, just beyond the end of the catwalk
The gargantua raises its sword; Noct begins to retreat back across the catwalk, but the daemon brings its sword down, shattering the catwalk and sending Noct into the depths of the Keep

text.SYSTEM: Zegnautus Keep
The height of imperial might, this flying megafortress houses the Crystal of Lucis in its uppermost level. Yet for all its imposing vastness, it appears utterly devoid of human presence.

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis comes to laying on his back at the bottom of the Keep's central shaft, surrounded by debris and the bodies of human imperial troopers; he slowly gets to his feet; as he takes a few steps, Noct comes upon Ravus's body, unceremoniously left here at the bottom level of Zegnautus Keep; as rumored, the last of the Oracle's bloodline is indeed deceased, his severed magitek arm still clinging to the haft of King Regis's glaive; the blade stands impaled in the floor beside Ravus's corpse; Noctis gazes at Luna's brother in silent sadness; after a moment, he reaches out toward the haft of his father's sword; at his touch, Ravus's severed arm falls to land on the first son of Tenebrae's chest; Noct pulls his hand back from the weapon, taking a moment to first kneel beside Ravus and look upon his face a final time; finally, Noctis stands, takes grasp of his father's royal arm, and pulls it free

text.SYSTEM: Sword of the Father x 1

text.Noctis: Rest easy. Your work is done.

text.NARRATIVE: As Noctis begins to walk out of the room across the narrow catwalk that serves as the only way out, a magitek trooper sprawled out on the floor of the catwalk rises to attack Noctis

text.Noctis: Well Dad, let's see what your sword can do.

text.SYSTEM: Noctis can now wield Regis's sword in combat.
Together with the Ring of the Lucii, it affords him a better chance of survival while his other abilities remain sealed.

text.NARRATIVE: As Noctis leaves the room, Ardyn can be heard laughing

text.Ardyn: Can't you simply taste the air of foreboding?
Did you hear that? There's something out there...

text.NARRATIVE: Shortly after Ardyn's ominous notice, the walls around Noctis begin spraying a green mist
Suddenly, Noct begins coughing and falls to one knee
If Noct tries to go from here down a hallway to the right, he will begin coughing, as it is being sprayed full of the green mist

text.Ardyn: A-ha! Well, you can't say I didn't warn you.

text.Noctis: Getting thicker by the second. Need to stop it.

text.SYSTEM: The poison gas reduces Noctis's HP.
Watch his health as you search for a way to clear the air.

text.NARRATIVE: Noct manages to locate a room with giant fans; operating the nearby control panel, he activates the fans, causing the poison gas to be sucked out of the area
He's then attacked by two snaga daemons

text.Ardyn: Oh, you're such a tease.

text.NARRATIVE: As Noct makes his way further, he comes to a storage room with yet another machine for updating security cards

text.SYSTEM: Card security clearance raised to level 4.

text.NARRATIVE: An automated message rings out

text.Announcement: Security clearance raised to level 4. Access to level 4 zones authorized.

text.NARRATIVE: Continuing onward, Noct fights his way through a room of several rogue axemen and shock trooper magitek troopers

text.Ardyn: You really are helpless without your friends babysitting you.
I have grave doubts about your friends.

text.NARRATIVE: Soon thereafter, Noctis opens the door to a room with an elevator

text.Ardyn: Tragedy could strike at any moment.

text.NARRATIVE: Noct presses the button to call for the elevator; while he is waiting for it to arrive, a large bat-like daemon called "Foras" descends behind and begins attacking him

text.SYSTEM: Wait while the elevator descends.

text.Noctis: Whatever the hell that is, I don't think I want to mess with it.

text.SYSTEM: The elevator has arrived.

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis uses the opportunity to escape; however, the Foras daemon will continue stalking him through the halls of the Keep
As Noctis gets off the elevator and begins making his way through the next hall before him, the lights go out

text.Noctis: Power must've gone out. First keys, now power. What next?

text.NARRATIVE: While Noctis navigates these dimly lit halls, Ardyn broadcasts his voice again

text.Ardyn: What was that noise? Is it scary being on your lonesome?

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis soon finds a power breaker and flips its switch, restoring some light to the area

text.Noctis: Ain't much, but it's better than nothing.

text.NARRATIVE: The Foras daemon begins manifesting in the halls of this area and attacking Noct

text.Ardyn: I love surprises! Oh, you'll fall for anything.

text.NARRATIVE: Going up a staircase to another level, the lights begin to flicker
Noctis must find yet another breaker, which he locates in a room with four magitek troopers resting within modules in the walls; he flips the switch, restoring some power

text.Noctis: Ain't much, but it's better than nothing.

text.NARRATIVE: He is then immediately attacked by two of the magitek troopers; and in the halls outside, Noct will again be beset by the Foras daemon
With power restored to the area, Noctis is able to take a nearby elevator up to the lab area of the Keep; as he begins making his way through the labs, Ardyn's voice is once again broadcast to Noct

text.Ardyn: The empire made considerable inroads into the science of daemons. Well, after I showed them the way, of course. We'd managed to make daemons... right here.

text.NARRATIVE: Noct soon locates a room full of control panels and learns how to navigate this area

text.SYSTEM: Different combinations of active circuits unlock specific sets of doors. To proceed, locate the keycard for each panel and activate the right combination.

text.Ardyn: Ever wonder where daemons come from? Once upon a time, they were children of nature—beasts and men. Aw, and you've killed so many.

The infantry units you callously dub "MTs" all began as babes in this very facility. Imprinted with serial codes and incubated until they were strong enough to fight. What a pity. Innocent souls fated to suffer... at the hands of a foreign king. Well, not so "MT" after all, are they?

text.SYSTEM: West Gralea Quarantine Report

Including cases around the village, the number of missing now stands at 1,657. Early reports from the MRF attribute the disappearance to an infectious disease, and investigations continue as regards a potential connection to the daemon outbreak. At the time of writing, the quarantining of West Gralea is complete, and other sections remain infection free.

text.NARRATIVE: Within the same room as the report, Noct is attacked by several snaga daemons before he can make his way through a door into the next hallway

text.Ardyn: Oho! Well done, my boy.

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn's laughter echoes through the area

text.Ardyn: The most fascinating tidbit about your dear Prompto...
Turns out he's not empty either. He's got quite the "skeleton in his closet."

text.NARRATIVE: Noct comes across and reads the Magitek Research Facility Damage Report in this lounge area

text.SYSTEM: Magitek Research Facility Damage Report

Following their outbreak in the north and west, daemons have swept through the MRF, causing extensive damage to equipment. Control was subsequently lost over unprogrammed MTs, and strategies are being deliberated on the collection of rogue units. 125 patients undergoing testing at the facility have vanished in a manner reminiscent of the first disappearances.

text.Noctis: All the patients up and disappeared? That makes no sense.

text.NARRATIVE: Noct soon locates another machine for updating security cards

text.SYSTEM: Card security clearance raised to level 5.

text.NARRATIVE: An automated message rings out

text.Announcement: Security clearance raised to level 5. Access to level 5 zones authorized.

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis is now able to enter an enormous open area with a wide, round platform at its center; a round, ornate single-room structure sits at the middle of this platform; along the walls of the large open space are countless small-paneled metal doors that make the walls resemble rows of lockers

text.Noctis: The hell is this place? What're they keeping inside?

text.NARRATIVE: Affixed to the ceiling above the structure in the middle of the room is a large apparatus emitting red electricity

text.Noctis: Not sure what that is, but I got a hunch it's bad. Don't like it one bit.
Bet there's something here. Which means it's locked. And if there's a lock, there's a key.

text.NARRATIVE: On the back of the structure, Noct finds a control panel with a switch; when he flips the switch, the platform begins rising

text.Noctis: Wasn't expecting that. Things are lookin' up.

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn interjects

text.Ardyn: How will this story end, I wonder.

text.NARRATIVE: An automated message rings out

text.Announcement: Intruder alert. Mobilizing dormant magitek infantry.

text.NARRATIVE: A swarm of magitek troopers begin leaping out of the panels along the walls

text.Noctis: What the—!? Wait... Is that what's waiting inside? Even more of 'em!

text.Ardyn: Where are your friends? You don't think (gasp) they ran off without you?
text._Subtitle: Whereare your friends? You don't think they ran off without you?

text.NARRATIVE: Note: the audio for this line has Ardyn pause and gasp mockingly after he says "think"

text.Ardyn: You still haven't found Gladio? Only a matter of time before Ignis bumbles into a trap. You must feel very much alone right now.

text.SYSTEM: (after the battle, Noct follows a catwalk leading away from the central platform and locates another machine that upgrades one's security clearance]
Card security clearance raised to level 6.

text.NARRATIVE: An automated message rings out

text.Announcement: Security clearance raised to level 6. Access to level 6 zones authorized.

text.NARRATIVE: Noct is then immediately beset once more by magitek troopers

text.Ardyn: Your buddies have bright lives ahead of them. Don't take it personally if they choose their own over yours.

text.NARRATIVE: After defeating the second wave of magitek troopers, Noct is confronted by a wraith daemon and more magitek troopers

text.Ardyn: Not so tough without your borrowed toys, are you?
You really are helpless without your friends babysitting you.

text.NARRATIVE: After the battle continues a little while longer, Ardyn's laughter rings out
The imperial chancellor's taunting continues as the battle goes on

text.Ardyn: Where does it hurt? You can tell me.

text.NARRATIVE: Once the wraith and all the magitek troopers have been destroyed, Noct is able to pass through a door into a new hallway, where Ardyn's laughter is soon heard; from here, Noct enters a room filled with control panels; on the other side of this room is the entrance to a hallway littered with the bodies of magitek troopers

text.Ardyn: In case there was any doubt: it's a trap.

text.NARRATIVE: Translucent, electrified doors close at either end of the hallway and begin closing in on Noctis; the magitek troopers also rise and begin attacking

text.Ardyn: A little pain never hurt anyone. On you go. Hurry. While you dawdle, people are dying.

text.Noctis: I've really gone and done it now.

text.NARRATIVE: Ignis's voice suddenly calls out from the other end of the hallway in the direction Noct had been going

text.Ignis: Noct? Is that you?

text.Gladiolus: Hey! Noct! Can you hear us?

text.Ignis: Where are you?

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio is able to see through the doors at the other end of the hallway and take stock of Noctis's situation; the doors have almost finished closing in on him now

text.Gladiolus: Noct's in trouble!

text.Ignis: Gladio! There ought to be a kill switch nearby—find it!

text.Gladiolus: How do you know that?

text.Ignis: I believe it's the reason we were brought here.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio finds the switch and is able to open the doors for Noctis; he leaps into the room with them and lets himself fall backward on the floor

text.Gladiolus: That was close.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio holds out his hand to Noct

text.Gladiolus: You're welcome?

text.NARRATIVE: Noct takes Gladio's hand, and Gladio pulls him to his feet

text.Ignis: After we were separated, we received "help"—from the usual suspect.

text.Gladiolus: That bastard's playing with us. But at least we're together.

text.Ignis: All but one of us.

text.Ardyn: Reunited with your retainers at last. How very touching. Must be a fine feeling, having friends. Look how happy you are! I pray you find your dear Prompto soon.

text.NARRATIVE: They free Prompto from the device he was being restrained to, and he falls to the floor; Noctis bends down to help him; Prompto has multiple bruises across his body; seemingly, he has undergone some degree of torture

text.Gladiolus: Hey, you alright?

text.Ignis: Are you hurt? Do you need help?

text.Prompto: I'm fine. Thank you, Noct.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto manages to sit upright

text.Prompto: Tell me. Were you worried about me?

text.NARRATIVE: A prompt appears to select either "Yeah" or "Not really"

CHOICE.Noctis: Of course I was. What kind of question is that?

CHOICE.Prompto: Of course. That's why you came, like I believed you would.
That's why I told myself I couldn't die. Not until I could see you and hear you tell me I'm not a fake—that I'm the real me.
Don't be. Everything's alright now.
Don't tell me you still think that I'm Ardyn.

CHOICE.Noctis: It's not like that. I knew the real you wouldn't kick the bucket so easily.

CHOICE.Prompto: I couldn't—at least not until I got to lay a guilt trip on you in person.

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: Prompto gets to his feet; Noctis stands as well

CHOICE.Prompto: The thought of that alone gave me the will to survive.
Don't be. Everything's alright now.

text.Ignis: Noct, do you hear that?
I've heard this sound before—on the train, just before your weapons failed you. It's nearby, and it may hold the key to restoring your power.
It's here.

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis stops at the large closed metal doors in the center of the enormous room
Noctis places his hand against the doors

text.Ignis: It's coming from within. Is there no way through?

text.Prompto: There's a way.

text.NARRATIVE: The others look at him; Prompto hesitantly steps up to the door's scanner and raises the back of his right wrist to it; the doors slide open; Prompto resumes speaking, staring off into the room, unable to make eye contact with the others

text.Prompto: So, MTs... They've got those codeprints... just like I do.
Yeah... So, as it turns out... I'm one of them. Not exactly something I could tell people growing up in Lucis.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto is fighting back tears, but continues speaking

text.Prompto: Still... You guys are like... the only friends I've ever known. I just hope that things can stay the way they were.

text.Noctis: Whatever. Who cares where you were born?

text.Ignis: I don't see you turning against us. Not now, or ever.

text.Prompto: Thanks, guys. Still... I can't change where I came from. What I am.

text.Noctis: Since when does where you come from matter to you? You never once treated me as a prince.

text.NARRATIVE: Noct playfully punches Prompto's shoulder

text.Gladiolus: He's got you there.

text.Ignis: Never so much as a "Highness."

text.Noctis: We're done here. C'mon, crown citizen.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio steps over to Ignis to help guide him into the room; he gives Prompto's shoulder a friendly smack as they walk past

text.Gladiolus: You're one of us, right?

text.NARRATIVE: Ignis stops and turns back toward Prompto over his shoulder

text.Ignis: Unless you'd rather not be.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto smiles, nods, and follows them

Inside the room Prompto opened, they find the emperor's abandoned clothing laying upon the throne; he, too, has become a daemon; they also find a large bank of computers, the cause of Noctis's lost powers; Noctis rams his father's sword through the machines

text.Prompto: So... did it work?

text.Ignis: With the device down and out, Noct's power should be up and running.

text.Gladiolus: Go on, try it.

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis holds out his hand and conjures a sword; Prompto claps in celebration

text.Gladiolus: We're back, baby.

text.SYSTEM: With all his powers restored, Noctis can once again travel to the past by calling Umbra at dormitories.

text.NARRATIVE: The gargantua daemon that caused Noct's earlier fall suddenly lands on the platform in front of them; it's quickly joined by other daemons, who begin manifesting

text.Prompto: New friend?

text.Gladiolus: You really need to pick 'em better.

text.Prompto: Iggy! Can you see again?

text.Ignis: ‘Fraid not, but that doesn't mean I can't fight.

text.Prompto: Well, just don't overdo it, okay?
I see you decided to rock the ring.

text.Noctis: Had to. No weapons, no friends, no choice, really. Y'know, somebody here's got to fight to rescue the Crystal... ... not to mention rescue all of your asses.

text.Gladiolus: Spoken like a true king. About time.

text.Ignis: The ring represents a great burden, but you don't bear it alone.

text.Noctis: You can say that again. Especially now that you all have your weapons back.

text.Gladiolus: Keep an eye on Iggy.

text.Prompto: I'll keep both on him!

text.Gladiolus: That'll do.
You really can hold your own.

text.Ignis: At the very least, I must try.
Hopefully Biggs and Wedge both made it to safety.

text.Prompto: Who and who?

text.Gladiolus: Our train drivers.

text.Noctis: And soldiers. They can fend for themselves.

text.Prompto: So, where'd you guys park the Regalia?

text.Gladiolus: Outside. Though "park" ain't the right word.

text.Ignis: She's broken down, alas.

text.Noctis: Took one for us, saved our lives.

text.Ignis: Now then, the Crystal.

text.Gladiolus: I'm guessing the way is locked.

text.Prompto: Well, I guess it's a good thing somebody has keys to the whole fortress.

text.Noctis: You're no better than a burglar.

text.Prompto: Aren't I?

text.Ignis: Truly be... the emperor?

text.Gladiolus: Does seem kinda keen on the ring.

text.Prompto: So we fight him?

text.Iedolas: The empire shall span... all the lands... By the Crystal's Light... we shall flourish... I shall arise... as ruler... of the world!

text.Gladiolus: One helluva hangar.

text.Prompto: Look at all this space.

text.Noctis: So, the central elevator's through here.

text.Gladiolus: And out of the loading bay.

text.NARRATIVE: The large doors at the other end of the hangar begin opening

text.Ardyn: Your Majesty, your precious Crystal awaits you. To liven things up I thought I'd take you on a stroll down memory lane. Of course, memories decay with time.

text.NARRATIVE: Ravus's body walks through the doors, now grotesque and daemonic, transformed into a monster

text.Ravus: Kill me... End it...

text.Gladiolus: Is that Ravus?

text.Prompto: Or what's left of him...

text.Gladiolus: A sorry end for the high commander—for anyone. He was a man with hopes and dreams.

text.NARRATIVE: Ravus's body begins to discorporate

text.Prompto: It's horrible.

text.Ignis: What kind of fiend makes daemons of men?

text.NARRATIVE: Ravus's body finishes discorporating and is gone; Noct looks sadly at the floor where his body had been

text.Gladiolus: Look alive—company!

text.NARRATIVE: The room suddenly fills with daemons; they begin to attack

text.Gladiolus: We're getting nowhere!

text.Prompto: And they just keep coming!

text.Ignis: Noct, you must go alone.
If you can obtain the Crystal's power, we may yet turn the tide. Elsewise, we are all like to perish here.

text.Gladiolus: Iggy's right. It's our only chance.

text.Prompto: We'll manage somehow! Just get moving!

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn broadcasts his voice to Noctis

text.Ardyn: You could still get to the Crystal... if you went on your own. Your friends will have to stay behind.

text.NARRATIVE: The elevator to the loading bay comes up to this level for Noct; he takes it down to the loading bay and begins running for the elevator on the other side
An automated message rings out

text.Announcement: Hangar gate closing Please stand clear.

text.NARRATIVE: The gate to the elevator begins to close

text.Ardyn: You'd better think fast. I don't envy you your decision.

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis continues to run as daemons begin manifesting and pursue him

text.Noctis: So this is the way to the Crystal?

text.Ardyn: Betraying your friends for the greater good—the mark of a monarch! Step forth, Your Majesty!
If you wish to obtain the Crystal's power, you must be prepared to lose all else.

text.NARRATIVE: Noct stops and looks back, seeing his friends absolutely swarmed by daemons, but fighting on; he turns to face the elevator, allowing the hangar gate to close behind him, separating him from his friends once again; he runs toward the final elevator

text.Announcement: Gate closed.

text.Ardyn: Do you suppose your dear friends are still alive? Those who died for you—do you ever wonder what went through their minds? Can you even recall their final words?

text.Noctis: I'll come back for you all. I swear.
How far's this go? The Crystal had better be here. Everyone's counting on it... counting on me.

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis runs into the room housing the Crystal; Ardyn broadcasts his voice to him once more

text.Ardyn: Your journey is over, Noct.

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis stands before the Crystal and holds his hand out to it

text.Noctis: Please... Help me stop the daemons.

text.NARRATIVE: Suddenly, the Crystal becomes very bright and seizes Noctis's hand; it begins to slowly pull him inside itself; as Noctis struggles in futility to get free, Ardyn swaggers into the room

text.Ardyn: Unharmed by the Light. The Chosen King, indeed. Allow me to regale you with a tale. In an age long past, an incurable scourge ravaged mankind. A tiny menace that twisted men into monsters, the likes of which you've seen. In Lucis lived a savior who could cure the afflicted. His body would come to host myriad daemons, that countless lives be spared. But a jealous king, one not yet chosen by the Crystal, ostracized and demonized this healer of the people. Making a true monster of him. I gave you my name earlier, but you should know that it was not the name given to me at birth. Ardyn Lucis Caelum is my proper name. You'll never guess whose name Izunia was. Noct, killing you as a mortal will bring me scant satisfaction. Claim the Crystal's power. Arise as its champion. Only once the Crystal and King are no more... can I know redemption. Come back soon. I shall keep your friends company until you are ready.

text.NARRATIVE: Note by Glenn Morrow: In the original Japanese script for what Ardyn says here, he reveals that the one named Izunia who betrayed him not only made a pariah of him, but also either executed him personally or caused his execution. The line that became "But a jealous king, one not yet chosen by the Crystal, ostracized and demonized this healer of the people" in the official English localization was が、まだクリスタルに選ばれていなかった王

text.SYSTEM: その 人々を救える 唯一の男を殺してしまった in Japanese.
A more direct translation of this would be "However, a king not yet chosen by the Crystal killed that only man who could save the people."]

text.NARRATIVE: After Noctis has been completely pulled into the Crystal, Prompto, Ignis and Gladiolus arrive, but are unable to do anything to help him; Ardyn turns to them, gestures nonchalantly at the Crystal and begins to walk away; Gladiolus swings his sword through Ardyn's head, releasing a puff of dark smoke from where the blade strikes; Ardyn falls back a little, but maintains his balance and holds onto his hat to keep it from falling off his head; he then continues walking away; Prompto shoots Ardyn in the back before he can take more than a couple of steps, releasing another puff of dark smoke and hurling his body onto the floor; Ardyn's hat rolls away and lays still for several seconds before Ardyn's hand suddenly reaches down to collect it and place it back on his head; once more unharmed, Ardyn is again standing; he smiles at Ignis, revealing corrupted daemonic features as he does so, but they go unnoticed since Ignis is blind; Ardyn walks away, leaving Noctis's closest friends unharmed but devastated

text.SYSTEM: Believing this sacred stone would purge the world of daemons, Noctis reached out to it, only to be pulled inside.

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis finds himself floating in an ethereal void resembling the Lifestream from Final Fantasy VII; he floats down into the palm of an enormous humanoid figure clad in dragon-like armor

text.Bahamut: Gather strength, O Chosen. The fate of this world falls to the King of Kings, His Providence consecrated in the divine Light of the Crystal. So it is ordained—the revelation of Bahamut.

text.SYSTEM: What is this place?

The heart of the Crystal, wherein lies the soul of the star, and it is in this place that the King will gain the power to fulfill his calling. By the covenants awakened, the Six have seen the coming of the prophesied hour—a time when the Crystal shall have shed the entirety of its Light unto the ring. Only then, once the sacred ring is replete, can the True King complete his ascension. And only by the True King's hand can the immortal Accursed be banished and the Light restored to this world.
Where are my friends?

text.Bahamut: They stand against the darkness and abide in hope, sustained by faith unfaltering that their King shall arise and bring deliverance.

text.SYSTEM: Who is "the Accursed"?

text.Bahamut: A man cursed with life eternal, whose immortality stems from the selfsame scourge that wrought the daemons. One so impure of body and soul was deemed unworthy of the Crystal's Light, and forbidden to ascend. His mind twisted by spite and bent on revenge, the Usuper came to bring darkness down upon our world. Only the True King, chosen by the Crystal and guarded by his forebears, can end the Accursed's madness.

text.SYSTEM: What is "Providence"?

text.Bahamut: It is the sole means to ending the immortal Accursed. A power greater than even that of the Six, purifying all by the Light of the Crystal and the glaives of rulers past. Only at the throne can the Chosen receive it, and only at the cost of a life: his own. The King of Kings shall be granted the power to banish the darkness, but the blood price must be paid. To cast out the Usurper and usher in dawn's light will cost the life of the Chosen. Many sacrificed all for the King; so must the King sacrifice himself for all.

text.NARRATIVE: Bahamut suddenly pulls his hand away and Noctis descends into the ether

text.Bahamut: Now enter into Reflection, that the Light of Providence shine within.

text.NARRATIVE: Note by Glenn Morrow: When Bahamut explains that the Lifestream-esque place Noctis finds himself in is "The heart of the Crystal, wherein lies the soul of the star," what he refers to as "the star" is 星 (i.e. hoshi) in Japanese; the word used for celestial bodies in general. It can mean "star," but can also refer to planets — and, indeed, is not only what everyone in FFVII refers to that game's planet by, but also what FFXV's Lore Guide from the game's opening tutorial explains the word to mean in this game

text.SYSTEM: In the Japanese version of FFXV, the segment of the Lore Guide entitled "The Six and the Oracle" ends with an additional line that says ちなみに、これらの話題でいう「星」は「世界」の意です — "By the way, ‘star' in these topics means ‘world.'" This either became "star" in the official English localization due to an error in translation or, as is more likely, a deliberate choice on the part of the localization to give some linguistic flair to the game's dialogue.
Click here for a screenshot or here for a video showing this segment of the Lore Guide in the Japanese version, and for further reference, this is Bahamut's line above in Japanese: 聖石の中　星の魂が宿そところ]

text.NARRATIVE: Additional note by Glenn Morrow: When Bahamut describes Ardyn with "One so impure of body and soul was deemed unworthy of the Crystal's Light, and forbidden to ascend," by "ascend" he means "become king." This turn of phrasing for the English localization, while elegant, is confusing, coming as it does right after "A man cursed with life eternal, whose immortality stems from the selfsame scourge that wrought the daemons.

text.SYSTEM: The reasonable implication to take from "deemed unworthy of the Crystal's light, and forbidden to ascend" is that it ties directly to Ardyn becoming "cursed with life eternal." In other words, that Ardyn cannot die and "ascend" because he became "one so impure of body and soul" that the Crystal rejects his soul returning to itself, the soul of the planet.

This understanding, while the reasonable conclusion to draw, is an unfortunate misunderstanding encouraged by the wording chosen here for the localization. What Bahamut actually says in Japanese is その汚れた身体を聖石に拒まれ王位に就くことなく葬られた愚かな男. A more direct translation of this would be "A foolish man who was rejected by the Holy Stone for that unclean body and was buried without ascending to the throne."
Ardyn's immortality, meanwhile, is a result of the Starscourge itself rather than due to the Crystal's rejection of him for absorbing the Starscourge.]

text.NARRATIVE: The screen briefly fades to black before revealing Noctis floating about in a meditative position; as he recalls memories from throughout his journey and from his childhood, the white light in the Ring of the Lucii on his hand grows ever brighter before briefly engulfing the whole screen

text.Bahamut: The Light waxes full. Go forth to the kingdom, where the Usurper awaits. Reclaim the throne, and fulfill the calling of the True King.

text.NARRATIVE: When the screen fades back in to reveal Noctis, he has disheveled facial hair and his youthful features have hardened; he's sitting inside a small stone structure and appears to slowly become aware of his surroundings as the white light emanating from the Ring of the Lucii fade

text.SYSTEM: Angelgard
Stone Prison

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis slowly rises to his feet and walks down a short series of steps to a beach outside where he finds Umbra waiting for him, a note in the dog's mouth
Noctis takes the note from Umbra and reads it

text.SYSTEM: Zegnautus Keep
At long last, the group infiltrates the imperial capital of Gralea, only to lose their king behind enemy lines. Gladiolus and Ignis storm Zegnautus Keep in pursuit of Noctis.

text.NARRATIVE: As the chapter begins, Gladio is pulling Ignis up to stand beside him on top of the train car that collapsed and separated them from Noctis

text.Gladiolus: Going up.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio places Ignis's cane back in his hand once they're both on top of the wreckage

text.Ignis: Is there a way forward?

text.Gladiolus: There's a way, but I don't see us going forward without facing off with the daemons.

text.Ignis: But now Noct is facing them alone. There must be some way we can help him.

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn's voice suddenly rings out

text.Ardyn: Perhaps I could be of service.

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn saunters out of the wreckage of another train car

text.Gladiolus: What are you doing here?

text.Ardyn: Why, I come bearing gifts.

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn snaps his fingers; as he does so, Gladio's sword materializes in his hand and a dagger materializes in Ignis's

text.Gladiolus: The hell?

text.Ardyn: See? Gifts! Now, I believe a "thank you" is in order.

text.Gladiolus: For what—another one of your stupid tricks?

text.Ardyn: Here I am, helping for a change, but I can see I'm not wanted.

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn gestures a farewell, turns, and walks away

text.Ignis: I'm loath to trust him.

text.Gladiolus: Same... but at this point, we need all the help we can get.

text.NARRATIVE: He looks at his sword for a moment before dispelling it; Ignis and Gladio begin to make their way down on the other side of the wrecked train car

text.Ignis: I ought to have been more cautious. If anything were to happen to Noct, I...

text.Gladiolus: Can't move forward if you're always looking backward. Quit thinking about what you could've done then and start thinking about what you can do now.

text.Ignis: You're right. What's done is done.

text.Gladiolus: So if we can conjure our weapons again, does that mean Noct can, too?

text.Ignis: I have a feeling the chancellor isn't so generous.

text.Gladiolus: How come?

text.Ignis: He may have feigned friendship, but he's proven a foe before. We'd best be careful.

CHOICE.Newscaster: This is the Imperial Security Bureau. A situation has arisen in several research sectors. All civilians must relocate to their designated refuge stations immediately. Failure to evacuate will result in incarceration or other appropriate disciplinary procedures. This emergency broadcast will repeat until the situation has been resolved. The Imperial Security Bureau thanks you for your cooperation.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: You think that "situation" is us... or something else?

CHOICE.Ignis: The latter, I presume. Whatever it is must be a matter of considerable scale to warrant such a warning. Keep your ears open. These broadcasts may help us understand what's going on outside.

text.Ignis: It's dead silent.

text.Gladiolus: More like undead silent. Place is crawling with daemons.

text.NARRATIVE: While they make their way through the Keep, Ardyn broadcasts his voice to Ignis and Gladio

text.Ardyn: Right this way, gentlemen.

text.Ignis: Proceed with caution.

text.Ardyn: Keep going... A little closer... Yes, that's a good boy.

text.NARRATIVE: A wall suddenly begins to slide open; Gladio holds his hand up to halt Ignis

text.Gladiolus: Hold up.

text.Ignis: What is it?

text.Gladiolus: Found some kinda secret passage.

text.Ignis: Lead here by our "guide"

text.Gladiolus: Long as it's a step in the right direction, I'll take it.

text.Ignis: Where are we now?

text.Gladiolus: Whatever it is, it's a mess. Watch your step.

CHOICE.Newscaster: This is a status report from the Imperial Defense Force. The daemon outbreak stemming from several research facilities has been suppressed in most areas. Magitek infantry units have been deployed to remaining sectors. The situation is under control. For your safety, a temporary curfew is imposed on all areas. Your cooperation is required to ensure the security of yourself and other civilians.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: They've got their hands full. Bet they never thought their little "pets" would bust outta their cages.

CHOICE.Ignis: I doubt even the daemons could simply escape from such a secure facility. It's more likely their "master" set them free.

text.Gladiolus: Hey, Iggy. Think we might've found the control room. Got lotsa... monitors and stuff.

text.Ignis: Which may help us monitor the rest of the keep. Does anything look operable?

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio begins examining a control panel

text.Gladiolus: I'm more of a low-tech kinda guy, but I'll see what I can do. What have we here? Huh. Looks like they wiped everything.

text.Ignis: All of it?

text.Gladiolus: Yep. Wait—I've got something. There's one surveillance tape they forgot to erase—almost like they wanted us to see it.

text.Ignis: Then we'd best have a look. Whatever's on that tape may help us locate Noct and Prompto.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladiolus plays the tape; a static-filled screen appears

text.Iedolas: What of the Hydraean's power? What of my precious ring?

text.NARRATIVE: The picture on the tape comes into focus; Ravus stands before the emperor in the throne room, King Regis's sword in hand; dark energy like that which rises when the daemons appear is rising off the emperor's hands

text.Ravus: By the hand of the Oracle, they are with the King now—their rightful owner. And someday soon, he shall use them to purge our star of its scourge.

text.Iedolas: But the Crystal is mine... I am the one True King!

text.Ravus: Nay, it is Noctis and none other.

text.NARRATIVE: Note by Glenn Morrow: When Ravus says "And someday soon, he shall use them to purge our star of its scourge," this line is a callback to earlier in the English localization when Lunafreya said "Only the true king, anointed by the Crystal, can purge our star of its scourge" — and as gone over there, what she referred to as "our star" there actually means the planet Eos

text.SYSTEM: For the Japanese version of this line from Ravus, all he actually says is "As the True King, he will certainly cleanse this world of its darkness." Here is the line in Japanese for further reference: いずれ真の王として必ずや世の闇を晴らしましょう]

text.NARRATIVE: Daemons begin coalescing behind Ravus; he turns his head slightly, taking notice of them

text.Ravus: Certainly not a puppet of the darkness and the daemons it has borne.

text.Iedolas: You are the puppet... and you must die.

text.NARRATIVE: The daemons begin to attack Ravus; he skillfully begins fending them off, wielding Regis's sword; a sudden blast of daemonic energy hits him from behind, though, pushing him out of the throne room and toward a railing; a second blast descends on him, but he is able to deflect it with the sword; a third blast, however, hits him squarely in the chest and launches him over the railing into the depths of the Keep; the picture on the tape descends into static again briefly before regaining focus, now with Ravus once more; he's pulling himself to his feet, holding to a railing and using King Regis's sword for support; he can barely stand; suddenly, what appears to be Noctis walks into the room; Ravus turns to him

text.Ravus: At last you have arrived, Noctis. The gods have shown you their favor. As Blood of the Oracle, I present you your father's glaive.

text.NARRATIVE: Ravus holds the haft of the sword out to him, gripping it with his magitek arm

text.Ravus: Now go forth, my king. Shine your light unto the world.

text.NARRATIVE: The one who appears to be Noctis begins to reach for the haft of the sword, then suddenly conjures a red-bladed facsimile of the Sword of the Father; he swings the sword at Ravus, cutting off his magitek arm just below the shoulder and seemingly injuring him elsewhere as well; Ravus takes a few clumsy steps forward, then collapses onto his back, dead; "Noctis" leans down and picks up the Sword of the Father, Ravus's severed arm still gripping it, then carries it over beside of Ravus's body; he shoves the blade into the ground, leaving it standing over Ravus

text.Noctis: Spare me your sycophancy. I've indulged your false heroism for far too long.

text.NARRATIVE: "Noctis" kneels down over Ravus's body and begins speaking with his real voice: Ardyn's

text.Ardyn: You tried to save the world in my stead, but it wasn't enough. The Crystal chose me—not you.

text.NARRATIVE: Now appearing as himself again, Ardyn stands and places his hat on his head before reaching into his coat and pulling out the letters Ravus had written to Lunafreya, discovered by Noctis in Chapter 13; Ardyn dismissively tosses the papers on Ravus's body, then begins walking out of the room

text.Ardyn: Aw, rejection hurts, doesn't it?

text.NARRATIVE: Note: The audio here has Ardyn say, "Aw, rejection hurts, doesn't it?"
The picture on the tape reverts to static; the scene reverts to Ignis and Gladio

text.Ignis: Was that Noct?

text.Gladiolus: No. Just that scumbag chancellor posing as him.

text.Ignis: It sounded like Ravus tried to return His Majesty's sword.

text.Gladiolus: Yeah. Guess he finally got over his grudge. Even called Noct "[his] king."

text.NARRATIVE: The two are silent for a moment

text.Gladiolus: Let's move. If that's what he did to Ravus, there's no telling what he'll do to Noct.

CHOICE.Newscaster: This is the Imperial Security Bureau. A state of emergency has been declared, effective immediately. Movement out of and around the city is restricted at this time. All civilians must relocate to their designated refuge stations and await further instruction. Civilians who fail to comply with official bureau directives will be subject to incarceration or other appropriate disciplinary procedures. This emergency broadcast will repeat until the situation has been resolved. The Imperial Security Bureau thanks you for your cooperation.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: They've got nowhere to run.

CHOICE.Ignis: And, at this point, no one left to protect them, either.

text.Gladiolus: Hey, there it is.

text.Ignis: What is it?

text.Gladiolus: The Crystal—right here on the screen.

text.Ignis: Then we're close. Do you see any sort of control panel?

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio examines the control panel

text.Ignis: If it's anything like the Citadel, there should be a barrier barring access.

text.Gladiolus: Then we un-bar it. You just tell me what to do.

text.Ignis: Right.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio begins to touch some of the instruments; the screen briefly fades to black; when it fades back in, Gladio is stepping back from the control panel, having just entered a command; he looks at the monitors in anticipation; the barrier blocking access to the Crystal turns off; suddenly, the foot of a daemon lands heavily on the floor behind Ignis and Gladio; they turn to face the creature; it's the Foras daemon from Chapter 13

text.Iedolas: Thieves cannot escape the hand of justice. The Crystal is mine... Never shall I lose my grip! The Crystal, the Light, the power... All of it... Mine!

text.NARRATIVE: As the daemon shouts that last word, the emperor's face is briefly superimposed over that of the creature; the daemon roars, preparing to attack; Ignis and Gladio conjure their weapons and fight back; after sustaining enough damage, the daemon growls, folds its wings over itself and vanishes in a puff of dark smoke; Gladiolus is breathing heavily

text.Ignis: I can't hear it anymore. Is it dead?

text.Gladiolus: Not yet—thing just disappeared. Ain't never seen one that talked like that before.

text.Ignis: Nor one so fixated on the Crystal.

text.Gladiolus: I thought Aranea said the daemons were afraid of the Crystal.

text.Ignis: It may be like moths to a flame—or it may be one of the empire's "alternative facts."

text.Gladiolus: Whichever it is, that monster's still on the loose.

text.Ignis: And we need to find it before it finds Noct and Prompto.

CHOICE.SYSTEM: Calling all frequencies—hey. Hey! Is anybody out there? ... Anybody who hasn't turned yet? Anybody? This is—no, forget it. What does it matter? Only a matter of time until I turn just like everyone else did. He was right. "Ain't long until the empire falls—and when she does, it'll hit like a ton of bricks." Should've taken his advice and got out when I had the chance. Y'hear that, Callux? You were right. Go on—tell me, "I told you so." Sorry I won't be able to pick up my tab.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Think anyone else heard that?

CHOICE.Ignis: If they did, I suspect they're no longer human enough to sympathize.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Whole place has gone to hell...
All the rest is probably just fake news.

CHOICE.Ignis: Assuming all of what we heard is true.

text.Gladiolus: If that son of a bitch even—

text.Ignis: Wait. Can't you hear that?

text.Gladiolus: Hear what?

text.Ignis: Noct's voice. I heard it clear as day. This way—follow me!

text.NARRATIVE: Ignis quickly sets out down the hall

text.Gladiolus: Hey, wait up!

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio takes off after him

text.SYSTEM: Noctis leaves his prison to find himself on Angelgard. His father's ship is moored at shore, none the worse for wear. It now carries him back to Galdin Quay—back to his kingdom.

text.Noctis: Man... How long was I out?

text.NARRATIVE: Noct and Umbra stand on the dock; even from here, Noct can already see that Galdin Quay is deserted and in shambles
As Noctis takes a few steps forward, daemons begin pouring out of the main venue at Galdin Quay and rush the dock

CHOICE.Noctis: This is it? This is all that's left of Lucis?

text.NARRATIVE: Umbra begins barking

text.Noctis: What is it, boy? Something's coming.

text.NARRATIVE: After a few seconds, a truck pulls into view around the bend and approaches
The vehicle pulls over and comes to a stop when it reaches Noct; he walks up to the driver's side door; the driver is a young man

text.Talcott: Uh...
It's me, Talcott. My grandpa served the Amicitia family?
Yeah.
Yes way. Welcome back, Your Majesty.

text.NARRATIVE: Talcott smiles; the scene transitions to inside the truck; Noctis and Umbra are now Talcott's passengers; Talcott is on the phone

text.Talcott: Yes, sir, that's—that's right. Hm? Oh. Just a second.
text._Subtitle: Yes, sir, that's right. Hm? Just a second.

text.NARRATIVE: Talcott hands the phone to Noct

text.Talcott: Said he wants to have a word with you?

text.Noctis: He can have it in person.

text.NARRATIVE: Talcott puts the phone back up to his own ear

text.Talcott: He said you can have it in person. Okay. We should be there shortly, sir.

text.NARRATIVE: Talcott begins to drive them all to Hammerhead; along the way, they pass a number of daemons prowling the land

text.Talcott: Wow. I can't tell you how good it is to see you again.

text.Noctis: Yeah. You sure look different, though.

text.Talcott: You think so? Guess I've grown some these ten years.
The guys must be pinching themselves right now.
Lestallum, more often than not, but they take a lot of trips to Hammerhead.
For Miss Cindy—y'know, back at the garage. She's a tough one, but when she needs a little extra muscle out on the road, she gives 'em a call.

Ah—speaking of which, the guys said they're near Hammerhead right now, so we'll be meeting them there. Y'know, ever since you disappeared, Your Majesty, it's been nothing but nighttime nonstop. Lestallum still has light—thanks to the power plant—so just about everyone's taken refuge there.

Everywhere else's been abandoned. Daemons moved in, forcing the people to move out. People still swing by the garage at Hammerhead from time to time, but it usually isn't for repairs. These days, it's less of a service station and more of a "slayer station"—a base for daemon-hunting. The garage's still open, though... one of the few places that is.

text.Noctis: So, um... Cid. Is he still alive and kicking?

text.Talcott: He's kicking alright, just not as hard as before. He hasn't really been himself lately. At lesat, not since he moved out to Lestallum. Someone suggested he move the garage there, too... ... but old man Cid wasn't having it. He called it "a big, fat chocobo turd of an idea." Said it just wouldn't be the same anywhere else.

Miss Cindy said she didn't mind either way, so the garage will probably stay put for a while. And without any tinkering to do, Ignig's gourmet seafood is about all Cid has left to look forward to. With all the daemons prowling around, more folk were getting hurt... or worse. So Iris talked the marshal into taking out the daemons themselves. "Iris the Daemon Slayer," they call her. Gladio and the others, they lend 'em a hand whenever they can. Prompto spends most of his time hunting around Hammerhead. He tries to impress Miss Cindy... but she's already married to her work.
He hunts, too. We tried to stop him, but he wouldn't listen. He said, if anything, he's more used to the darkness than we are.

text.Noctis: Never did get his vision back...

text.Talcott: I'm afraid not. But, that being said, he gets by pretty well on his own. Gladio and Prompto usually hunt on their own as well. It isn't often you see the three of them together nowadays. They still work as a team every once in a while, but each has his own set of tasks to keep him busy.
We've arrived, Your Majesty. Everyone'll be so happy to see you. Don't worry—I won't be going anywhere. If you have any other questions, please don't hesitate to ask.

text.NARRATIVE: Talcott drives through the new perimeter gate at Hammerhead, then parks near Takka's Pit Stop; Ignis, Prompto and Gladio are standing there, waiting; Noct gets out and walks over to them

text.Gladiolus: "Hey"? That's all you have to say for yourself—after all this time?

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio puts his hand on Noct's shoulder and playfully shoves him

text.Prompto: Noct, it's you! It's really you!

text.Ignis: Well, well. You kept us waiting.

text.NARRATIVE: Noct walks up to Ignis and places his hand on his shoulder; Ignis smiles

text.Noctis: Not like I wanted to. We've got catching up to do.

text.Ignis: Let's head inside.

text.NARRATIVE: The four friends walk toward Takka's Pit Stop

text.SYSTEM: The final battle will commence once you leave Hammerhead.
Be sure to spare no preparation.

CHOICE.Talcott: I'm more than happy to tell you everything I know.
We've even got some former imperials fighting for us. The toughest of 'em said she used to lead a band of mercenaries.

So you do know her. I'm not surprised; the marshal said she used to be feared far and wide back in the day. But now she's revered among the Lucian masses—same with her men, Biggs and Wedge. Each of them leads their own small army.
Oh, right—about the empire.
Gladio brought back word that both the emperor and high commander were dead. With those two gone, Niflheim pretty much fell apart.

The chancellor's still around, though... in Insomnia. Nobody who saw him had any clue what he might have been up to, but their stories piqued Ignis's curiosity. I ended up helping Ignis look into the matter—digging through old records, even joining him on trips to the royal tombs.
It's cool—I'm a bit of a history buff myself. But we did discover something pretty weird.

While we were poring over all those ancient texts, one name caught our eye: Ardyn's. Apparently he was hailed as a savior, healing all those who were ravaged by daemons... ... only to end up branded a daemon himself—a dubious charge, I'd say. By all accounts, he was just as human as you and me.

On the bright side, we've come a little closer to understanding the daemons. Y'see, I'd always thought they were animals, only more hideous and savage. But... it turns out they're just ordinary people... ... unlucky folk infected by something or other that transformed them into monsters. There's no known cure as of yet, so death is the only mercy.

CHOICE.SYSTEM: We've got a lot of survivors pouring in from Accordo, too, what with all the daemon attacks there as of late. Not like it's much better here. Lestallum's practically overflowing with refugees from Insomnia. The empire's "recovery assistance" fell by the wayside, and daemons overran the city. Thankfully, Iris and the marshal managed to evacuate the civilians. Now there's no one left... except the daemons. I spent my childhood in the Crown City. It's sad knowing it's gone, y'know?

CHOICE.Noctis: Not for long. I became the king to reclaim our home, and now I'm back—as promised.

CHOICE.Talcott: All these years, and you remembered.
Your Majesty... do you remember my grandfather?

There's something I wasn't able to tell you back then. Grandpa died because of me... It was my fault. An imperial officer approached me in town, asked if I was from the Crown City. And that was just the beginning: "What brings you here, young man? You didn't come here by yourself, did you?" "Your grandfather is a butler at a manor? How very grand!" "He rubs shoulders with the royal family? You must be ever so proud!" I answered him without thinking. A little after that, the man showed up at our hotel.
Think what you will of me, but please know that Grandpa didn't give you away.
Yeah?

CHOICE.Noctis: You're not a kid anymore. You should know by now what happened that day wasn't your fault—none of it. Y'know, it's hard to ask someone about their pain, but it's just as hard to share your own with someone else. I appreciate you opening up to me, and I swear I'll make things right. But believe me when I say nobody blames you. Not me, not your grandpa. Trust me: you have the king's word.

CHOICE.Talcott: I suppose you're right, Your Majesty. Thank you.

CHOICE.Noctis: So Ignis, you're really cooking like you used to.

CHOICE.Ignis: More or less. I can manage with far less help than I required before.

CHOICE.Prompto: Y'know, it's okay to ask for help. You don't need to prove anything to us.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Probably more about proving it to himself. I say we leave him to it.

CHOICE.Prompto: Yeah, I guess that's how he got so good. Even better than before, if you can believe it.

CHOICE.Ignis: Perhaps I've developed a culinary sixth sense.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Hey, Iggy. You oughta follow Weskham's example, open up a restaurant.

CHOICE.Ignis: I'll give the matter some thought—assuming such demand still exists in a post-apocalyptic world.
Prompto's even capable of hunting alone these days. He really has come a long way.

CHOICE.Prompto: Had to become a functioning adult sooner or later.

CHOICE.Noctis: Doesn't feel like you've changed, though.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Not nearly as much as he claims.

CHOICE.Prompto: You gonna spoil my moment?

CHOICE.Gladiolus: What's there to spoil?

CHOICE.Noctis: Y'know, even after all this time, you guys haven't changed.

CHOICE.Ignis: Not as individuals, perhaps, but we no longer need to ask one another for help in times of need. We've reached the point where that sort of synergy is second nature.

CHOICE.Prompto: Yeah, and it only took us ten years to get here.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: So yeah, no wedding just yet.

CHOICE.Prompto: No wedding ever.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Hey, don't hate me.

CHOICE.Prompto: "Hate the game." Yeah, yeah.

CHOICE.Ignis: So we can't expect a formal introduction for some while, then.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Yeah. At least not 'til all of this is over. Can't in good conscience leave a girl to worry while I rush headlong into danger.

CHOICE.Prompto: Gee, you oughta teach a master class in romance.

CHOICE.Ignis: Or acting.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: No acting here. I keep it real with the ladies.

text.NARRATIVE: A prompt appears asking "Return to Insomnia?"; the player can select either "Yes" or "No"

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: The four have now walked outside the gate

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Well, fellas, we're homeward bound at last. Time to suit up.

CHOICE.Prompto: Finally get to rock these threads.

CHOICE.Ignis: Wear them with pride.

CHOICE.Noctis: Yeah, just hope they still fit.

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: The four make camp on the same hill overlooking Insomnia where they once bore witness to the imperial invasion; Ignis cooks their dinner, just as he did in the old days

CHOICE.SYSTEM: After ten long years of solitude, Noctis is reunited with his friends. Breaking camp for the final time, they return to the Crown City of Insomnia, where the Chosen King will make his stand and restore the Light to the world.

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: Noct and his retinue walk into view, prepared to fight their way to the Citadel in the heart of Insomnia; he now wears the Kingly Raiment, as he did in the game's opening sequence during the battle with Ifrit; likewise, the others wear the uniform of the Kingsglaive

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Home, sweet home.

CHOICE.Prompto: Yeah, at long last.

CHOICE.Ignis: What we've been waiting for...

CHOICE.Prompto: Sure is.

That's right—you have the power of kings flowing through your veins. You're the only one I'd trust this key to. No one else.
Those seals are bound to break sooner or later. It's better to strike first, on our own terms.
Listen up. Death lurks behind every one of those doors. You must go prepared.
