CHOICE.Gladiolus: So what—the weak aren't worthy of serving as Shield?

CHOICE.Cor: In his eyes, the weak aren't worthy of living. All of them are fools, punished for aspiring beyond their station. I was a fool back then, too—and I was punished.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: But you weren't killed. Maybe you weren't worthy of serving as Shield, but he must've seen you as worthy of living.

CHOICE.Cor: Maybe he did, maybe he didn't.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: No point in overthinking it.

CHOICE.Cor: But don't forget it.

text.Cor: Keep your eyes and ears open.

text.Gladiolus: Done and done.

text.NARRATIVE: The spirit from before continues projecting its voice to Gladio

text.Soul: Your skill is impressive. You may have the strength to defeat the darkness... ... but do you have the spirit to survive these trials?

text.Gladiolus: Not good—they keep on coming!

text.Cor: Just like I taught you. Ready?

text.Gladiolus: And raring to go!

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio and Cor come to a wall made of rock formations curved inward on one another; it is also seemingly sealed by a magical talisman consisting of a sword stuck in the ground with several ropes tied to it; the sword's blade glows with blue energy

text.Gladiolus: What's this?

text.Cor: A trial chamber. The hand-holding stops here—good luck.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio grabs the grip of the sword, and the ropes vanish in a flash of light; he pulls the blade from the ground and the entire weapon then vanishes in a burst of light; the rock wall crumbles away, revealing a small cave; Gladiolus enters and is confronted by a host of skeletons and a wraith-like entity called a nergal as the cave wall behind him becomes sealed once again

text.Soul: Prepare yourself, Young Warrior, for the trial that awaits. Prove your might, and our power shall be yours.

text.NARRATIVE: He approaches a small shrine made from rocks within the chamber; inside burns a blue flame; Gladio places his hand on the flame and endures the subsequent winds and energy that buffet him from within the shrine; he then pulls his hand out of the shrine; his hand now briefly burns with the blue flame

text.Soul: Our power goes with you now, Young Warrior.

text.NARRATIVE: The rocks the shrine is made from turn to light and vanish as the wall behind the shrine splits and slides open to allow Gladio further passage

text.SYSTEM: Gladiolus has completed the first of the souls' trials.
He can now perform blocks capable of withstanding the mightiest of blows—even those dealt by the Blademaster himself.

text.Soul: Stand tall, for the Shield of the King must kneel in subjugation before no man.

text.NARRATIVE: Cor rejoins Gladio at this point

text.Gladiolus: Thanks for the advice—and for the pick-me-up.

text.Cor: Well, you made it out alive. Your first trial may have ended, but many more await you on your road to an audience with the Blademaster. Prepare yourself.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio and Cor soon emerge from the cavern onto a ledge along the cliffside within the Talepar Crag; there's a campsite here

CHOICE.Gladiolus: My father never undertook the Trial of Gilgamesh, did he?

CHOICE.Cor: No. You wanna know why?

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: A prompt appears to select either "Yeah" or "Not really"

CHOICE.Gladiolus: I do. I mean, it can't be because he was scared, right?

CHOICE.Cor: Not of the Trial. He was scared of failing as leader of the Crownsguard—and as Shield of the King. He couldn't leave His Majesty alone, weakened by the Wall as he was. After all, what good is a Shield with no one to protect? What about you? Worried about leaving Your Majesty alone?

CHOICE.Gladiolus: A little, but I'm gonna do what's right for me like my father did what was right for him.
He never pried into my business, so I won't dig into his.

CHOICE.Cor: Like father, like son.

text.NARRATIVE: From the ledge with the campsite, the path ahead is a ramp running up the face of the cliffside; the ramp appears to be made of wood that has long-since rotted, but it holds; it also leads to two other such ramps, which allow the two warriors to gradually ascend along the cliffside

text.Gladiolus: How long has it been since you undertook the Trial? Thirty years or so?

text.Cor: Give or take. I was a lot younger than you are—and far less experienced. It's a wonder I even made it out alive.

text.Gladiolus: This place look familiar to you?

text.Cor: Vaguely. The younger me had little mind for taking in the sights.

text.NARRATIVE: Before long, Gladio and Cor reach additional wooden pathways, which they follow to an actual stone path along the cliffside; from there, they reach the entrance to another cavern within the cliff wall; after disposing of the creatures that attack them by the entrance, they proceed into the cavern
Gladio and Cor come across a talisman and wall similar to the one from earlier

text.Gladiolus: Another trial chamber.

text.Cor: And another chance for the warriors to impart their wisdom. It won't come easy, though—you'll have to earn it.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio proceeds to the new trial chamber in the same manner as the first, only this one is actually a stone bridge spanning the divide of the Taelpar Crag; as Gladio walks out onto the stone bridge, he looks up to find himself being targeted by a fiery winged creature called an enkidu

text.Soul: How many moons has it been?
Since our last visitor? Far more than I can count.
Let us see how our latest challenger will fare.

text.SYSTEM: (once Gladio defeats the enkidu, he proceeds across the bridge and climbs through a fissure in the cliff wall to enter a stone chamber housing the next power shrine; akin in design to the first, Gladio proceeds in like manner]

text.Soul: Venture forth, Young Warrior, bearing our hopes and dreams.

text.NARRATIVE: This shrine vanishes in the same fashion as the first, and the wall beyond it likewise splits and slides open as before

text.SYSTEM: Gladiolus has completed the second of the souls' trials.
He can now perform the Maelstrom Glaive Art when his valor is high.

text.Soul: Look ahead, for the Shield of the King must safeguard our future.

text.Gladiolus: Leave it to me.

text.NARRATIVE: He's now rejoined by Cor

text.Soul: The skills shared by these souls have been passed down for generations. The Shield of the King would do well to put them to good use.

text.Gladiolus: Gotta say, this place ain't like anywhere else in Lucis.

text.NARRATIVE: After defeating all the enemies in this room, an exit back to the cliffside is revealed as part of the wall splits and slides open

text.Soul: Thousands set foot on these grounds, all of them fools unprepared for the dangers lurking within. They all meet with the same fate—as will you.

text.Gladiolus: I don't think so.

text.Soul: Think what you may, but I know otherwise. The Lucis you call home is nothing like the Lucis I once served. Your age has forgotten the horrors of war, coddled by the king and drunk off the complacency of peace. No Shield worthy of defending the True King could be born from such depravity.

text.Gladiolus: Thanks for the vote of confidence.

text.Cor: Look at the bright side: everyone loves an underdog.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio and Cor proceed across another wooden path, then down another series of wooden ramps, eventually coming to a second stone bridge spanning the chasm; several large creatures are on the bridge

text.Gladiolus: Aww. A warm welcome, just for me.

text.Soul: Will you stand tall, even when your flesh fails you, or will you fall to your knees?

text.NARRATIVE: After reaching a higher ledge, battling some more large creatures, and then ascending more wooden ramps, Gladio and Cor find another campsite on a ledge

text.Gladiolus: Time to take a load off.

CHOICE.Cor: Never thought I'd make my way back to the Tempering Grounds.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: You said it's been thirty years. Were you as "immortal" then as you are now?

CHOICE.Cor: If you wanna know, I'll talk.

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: A prompt appears to select either "Yeah" or "Not really"

CHOICE.Gladiolus: The Blademaster—what was he like?

CHOICE.Cor: I don't remember much... except for those eyes. They pierced my heart and peered right into my soul. It was like he knew my every move even before I did. Try as you may, there's no fooling those eyes.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: We'll see about that.
Nah, I'm fine not knowing.

CHOICE.Cor: Some stories are better left untold.

text.NARRATIVE: From the campsite, Gladio and Cor enter another cavern passageway within the cliff face

text.Soul: He who protects the king... ... must boast muscle and mettle, both finely tempered. Should he lack either, the Shield will shatter.

text.NARRATIVE: Shortly thereafter, the two warriors come to a wall upon which a demonwall-like entity manifests; this being is called an inannaduru, and is accompanied by soul of fortitude enemies
The creature discorporates and the wall it had been bonded to shatters

text.Cor: The penultimate trial awaits. Prove to them you're prepared to serve as the Shield of the Chosen King.

text.NARRATIVE: Soon thereafter, Gladio and Cor find the next trial chamber, one much like the first

text.Soul: Be true, for the Shield of the King must deceive none—not even himself.

text.Gladiolus: Yeah, easier said than done.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio enters the trial chamber, emerging into a short cavern passageway; after making his way down a couple of stone stairways, he finds himself in a room with another shrine; suddenly, a large creature resembling the red giant daemons begins to manifest; called a humbaba, it also manifests in the same manner as those daemons

text.Soul: The Shield is bold, shrinking before none. Waste not the arsenal at your behest.

text.NARRATIVE: When Gladio defeats the humbaba, it discorporates like a red giant daemon as well; Gladiolus then claims the power in the nearby shrine as he has during previous trials

text.Soul: Now, naught but the final trial awaits you.

text.NARRATIVE: As has been the case after claiming the power at previous shrines, the wall behind this one likewise splits and slides open

text.SYSTEM: Gladiolus has completed the third of the souls' trials.
An aura envelops his blade, allowing him to deal damage to Gilgamesh.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio is rejoined by Cor

text.Cor: Nice work. Maybe you've got what it takes after all.

text.Gladiolus: Maybe, but it ain't for you or me to decide.

text.Cor: True—and the Blademaster is a more formidable foe than any you've faced thus far.

text.NARRATIVE: Venturing through the new opening, Gladio and Cor find another campsite

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Well, what about you? I wanna know what was going through your head back then.

CHOICE.Cor: You that interested in me?

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: A prompt appears to select either "Yeah" or "Not really"

CHOICE.Gladiolus: I mean, you were a lot younger than I am.

CHOICE.Cor: And a lot brasher too, if you can believe it. Wouldn't listen to a single word anyone said. I thought I was invincible. No one could stop me... until he cut me down to size. I was cast out in defeat, my hubris laid bare for all to see. "You really are immortal," they said—and it stuck.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: That's rough... Still, you made it back alive—something no one else has ever done—and I respect that.
Don't flatter yourself. Forget I even asked.

CHOICE.Cor: It would be my pleasure.

text.Soul: Come here to die, have you?

text.Gladiolus: You looking to die again?

text.Soul: You amuse but do not impress. You lack his conviction.

text.Gladiolus: Whose?

text.Soul: He who traversed these caves some thirty years ago. Turning a deaf ear to our wails and wishes, he proceeded unfazed, eyes ever forward. Yet he proved powerless before the general, cast out in defeat. If even he could not succeed, I see no hope for you.

text.Cor: That guy must've left quite an impression... ... when he landed flat on his face.

text.NARRATIVE: Making their way down to yet one more ledge, Gladio and Cor soon find themselves at a sealed wall in the cliff face; unlike previous trial chambers, this one is not sealed by a talisman, just rock growth; Cor stands before the wall, and raises his katana, still in its sheath; he unsheathes the blade a foot or so; the rock growth barring Gladio's entry dissipates; Cor sheathes his katana once more and lowers the weapon; he speaks to Gladio without turning to look at him

text.Cor: Clarus would've tried to stop you, you know—just like he tried to stop me all those years ago.

text.Gladiolus: How come?

text.Cor: Because one aspiring to the role of King's Shield can stake his life for none but his liege—not even for himself.

text.NARRATIVE: Cor looks at Gladio

text.Cor: "Do you dare risk all for naught in return?" His words stayed with me. And he was right: I barely made it back with nothing to show for it.

text.Gladiolus: So, you gonna stop me?

text.Cor: No, I won't. But I will warn you one last time of the danger you're about to face—just like your father warned me. Once you set foot through that door, there's no turning back—and no one to help you if you fall. One false step, and it may prove your last.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio takes a couple of steps forward

text.Gladiolus: I'll be fine. Maybe I'll come back with a souvenir.

text.NARRATIVE: He smiles at Cor, then proceeds on ahead

text.Cor: Just come back alive. Be safe, Gladio.

text.Gladiolus: There's a chill in the air... I can feel his presence. He'd better be ready for me.

text.NARRATIVE: He comes to a final stone bridge spanning the Talepar Crag; embedded in the stone bridge on either side along its full length are a great multitude of swords; Gilgamesh stands at the other end of the bridge, his back turned; Gladio approaches and announces himself

text.Gladiolus: I'm here.

text.NARRATIVE: Gilgamesh slowly turns his head

text.Gladiolus: Yeah. Let's see if you can handle it.

text.NARRATIVE: Their battle begins; Gilgamesh wields a broadsword in the hand of his only remaining arm

text.Gilgamesh: You only delay the inevitable, O Unworthy One. Look how you tremble!

text.Gladiolus: I ain't afraid of you.

text.Gilgamesh: With every passing second, the fear in your heart grows greater still.

text.Gladiolus: So what do I do? Just roll over and die?

text.Gilgamesh: Yes. Why else would you have come here, if not to join the other lost souls?

text.Gladiolus: Because I've got what it takes—and I'm gonna prove it!

text.NARRATIVE: At a certain point in the battle, Gilgamesh parries Gladio's sword, then simply stands and stares

text.Gilgamesh: Blind reliance on strength alone reveals your weakness of will.

text.NARRATIVE: As Gilgamesh utters his next line, Gladio turns to look across the many blades found here

text.Gilgamesh: Countless disappointments met their end here, and so shall you!

text.SYSTEM: Gladiolus; No. I didn't come here to die. I came here to prove to you I'm worthy!

text.NARRATIVE: At a certain point, Gladio seemingly has Gilgamesh defeated and brings his blade down for a bisecting swing intended to finish him off; Gilgamesh forms a fiery left arm from his energy, however, and catches Gladio's blade

text.Gilgamesh: You are strong—yet so long as fear binds your heart... ... the power you possess is wasted on you.

text.NARRATIVE: Gilgamesh dispells the broadsword in his right hand and replaces it with a katana that he begins to wield in both hands

text.Gladiolus: I've still got some tricks up my sleeve, too.
text._Subtitle: I've still got a few tricks up my sleeve, too. Ain't no way I'm backing down now!

text.NARRATIVE: After depleting half of Gilgamesh's remaining energy, Gladio will attempt a horizontal slash across Gilgamesh's midsection; Gilgamesh blocks the attack, however, and counters with a slash that cuts Gladio across his forehead; this is the origin of the new scar Gladio carries when he returns to Noctis and the others in Chapter 8 of the main game; eventually, Gladio is able to defeat Gilgamesh, delivering a strike that throws Gilgamesh off balance and down onto one knee; his fiery left arm dissipates as he falls

text.Gladiolus: I kneel before no man!

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio just stares at Gilgamesh for a moment, then seems to become aware of the pain in his forehead, grunting a couple of times and placing his hand there; he lets out a chuckle

text.Gladiolus: Not exactly the "souvenir" I had in mind. It took me a while, but I realized something: you're right—I am afraid. Afraid of accepting the fact that maybe I'm not really cut out for the job I'm expected to do. But hey, at least I'm not walking away empty-handed. I'd better get going. I may be all muscle and no mettle, but I'm gonna keep protecting Noct the only way I know how.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio turns and starts walking away; Gilgamesh rises back to his feet and addresses him

text.Gilgamesh: Spoken like a true Shield of the King.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio stops and turns back to face the undead warrior

text.Gilgamesh: Fear and doubt beget death alone. He who averts his gaze from his own faults cannot himself a true Shield call, but you—having made peace with your inner self—have proven you are worthy. The Chosen King should be so fortunate as to have a man like yourself serving at his side.

text.Gladiolus: You mean... ?

text.NARRATIVE: Gilgamesh looks at his katana, then holds its grip out to Gladio

text.Gilgamesh: And with this glaive, I entrust my power to you.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio stabs his own sword into the ground, then approaches Gilgamesh to receive his gift, the Genji Blade; as he takes the weapon into his hands, Gladio notices a medallion bearing the Crownsguard symbol hanging from the katana

text.Gladiolus: Where did you... ?

text.Gilgamesh: Taken from the young man who impressed me with his strength of will. It was with this very blade he stole from me my arm.

text.Gladiolus: But... I can't accept this.

text.Gilgamesh: If he still walks among the living, a man of his mettle will have doubtless transcended attachment to mere material possessions.

text.Gladiolus: You're probably right. In that case, don't mind if I do.

text.Gilgamesh: Now, hasten forth—with mind unclouded by doubt and will unmoved by fear. The Last King of Lucis is ill fit to fight without his Shield.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio nods and smiles

text.Gladiolus: Thanks again.

text.NARRATIVE: He turns and leaves, carrying the Genji Blade at his side

text.Cor: You made it.

text.Gladiolus: Sure did.

text.Cor: And so quickly. I'm impressed.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio raises the Genji Blade, and shows it to Cor

text.Gladiolus: Brought this back with me, too. Figured you might get a kick out of it.

text.Cor: I wondered where I put that thing.

text.NARRATIVE: Cor stares at it for a moment, then realizes Gladio is presenting it to him

text.Cor: Keep it. Makes for a better souvenir than that scar.

text.NARRATIVE: Cor turns and begins to walk away; Gladio follows after; the scene transitions to the two walking back down the path they took into the Tempering Grounds

text.Gladiolus: Y'know, he mentioned he lost his arm in battle with a real hot-headed young guy back in the day.

text.Cor: That so?

text.Gladiolus: Whoever it was left a lasting impression on him. Talked about how the guy had the strongest will he'd ever seen.

text.Cor: Takes more than will to complete the trial. You need to wield your weapon with a primal finesse. If you fail to prove your might, you get cast out empty-handed.

text.Gladiolus: I dunno. He didn't seem to think the guy would let it bother him. Said the guy's too old to care about material things anymore—if he's still alive.

text.NARRATIVE: The scene transitions to the two walking back out into the wider world

text.Cor: Gladio.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio comes to a stop, then turns back to Cor

text.Gladiolus: Huh?

text.Cor: I hope you feel more confident in light of your success today. Few men can lay claim to such an accomplishment—not even Cor the Immortal.

text.Gladiolus: Yeah, but I didn't earn myself a badass nickname like he did. Still, I'm glad I went through with it.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio turns back to the outside world

text.Gladiolus: I can finally say I'm truly ready to fulfill my duty.

text.Cor: Good.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio stretches his shoulders

text.Gladiolus: Well, I guess this Shield better mosey on back to his King. Wouldn't want him to get scared without me.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio and Cor continue on; the screen fades to black for a long moment, then transitions back to the time of Chapter 8 in the main game, with Gladio finishing up his story

text.Prompto: So that's how you got it.

text.Gladiolus: Whaddaya think?

text.Prompto: Very perpendicular. Really complements the one you got when you saved Noct from that bully.

text.Gladiolus: Yeah. Only difference is, this time, I ended up taking a pretty bad beating, too.

text.Ignis: Not unlike the licking the marshal received back when he was a lad.

text.Prompto: Musta had a lotta guts to go up against Gilgamesh back then.

text.Noctis: Yeah, Dad said he used to be a real firecracker.

text.Prompto: The more you know...

text.NARRATIVE: Ignis looks down, as though pondering, and makes a "Hm" sound

text.Ignis: If the Blademaster sequestered himself during the Founder King's reign, then he's haunted those halls for some two millenia.

text.Prompto: That's a long time.

text.Gladiolus: All those years waiting for the Chosen King to arise. You sure know how to take your sweet old time.

text.Noctis: What can I say? I'm worth the wait.

text.Prompto: Gimme a break.

text.Ignis: And I, as well.

text.Gladiolus: Just because you've got a Shield to protect you now doesn't mean you get to slack off.

text.NARRATIVE: Gladio leans back in his chair, then looks at the Genji Blade propped up beside him and smiles

text.Gladiolus: But if you do, I'll be ready.

text.NARRATIVE: The screen fades to black

CHOICE.Cor: Congratulations, Gladio. You accomplished that which I couldn't. Care to show this failure how it's done?

CHOICE.Gladiolus: First the Blademaster and now the Immortal? I can't catch a break.

CHOICE.Cor: Not on my watch. Ready?
At ease. Thus ends your final "trial." You did Clarus proud today. Now go. Walk tall as the Shield of the Chosen King.

text.SYSTEM: A schism splits the royal retinue when Noctis inadvertently pushes Prompto from atop a speeding freight liner. Seemingly betrayed by his best friend, Prompto suppresses feelings of sadness and trudges through the snow in search of answers.

text.NARRATIVE: The episode opens on Prompto slowly making his way across a snowfield during a blizzard, his left arm raised to shield him from the wind and snow; since being separated from his friends, he's also donned attire more appropriate for this environment, such as a fur-lined jacket and boots, as well as a skull cap; even with these measures at protecting himself from the cold, he grunts with each step, and ice has formed on his hair and face; a caption informs us that this is "Several days later... " following his fall from the train in Chapter 11 of the main game

text.Prompto: It's freezing out here.

text.NARRATIVE: After taking a few more steps, Prompto begins having great difficulty just remaining on his feet

text.Prompto: No...

text.NARRATIVE: After barely making it any further, Prompto gasps and collapses to his knees; after managing to get back up, he continues shuffling forward, more slowly than before

text.Prompto: What a way to go.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto makes it no more than a couple of steps further before collapsing face first into the snow with a weak grunt; as the elements continue their relentless assault upon him and his vision begins to fade, Prompto looks up to see imperial soldiers jumping down onto the snowfield from drop ships above; the soldiers stand over Prompto, examining him as his body succumbs and his awareness fades to white
A vision plays of Prompto as a child walking across the courtyard outside the Citadel with his eyes cast down; Prompto's voice can be heard

text.Prompto: My whole life, all I ever wanted was friends...

text.NARRATIVE: The vision of Prompto as a child looks up to see Gladio, Ignis and Noct as adults coming down the steps of the Citadel, then walking past him across the courtyard; they seemingly don't even notice him

text.Prompto: ... but no one ever wanted me back.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto watches them go, then hangs his head

text.Prompto: So when I finally found people who [I]did[/I] want me, I did everything I could to make them stay.

text.NARRATIVE: Young Prompto starts to run after his friends, but they vanish; he hangs his head once more, and turns to walk back toward the Citadel steps once again

text.Prompto: And ever since then, I've lived my life in fear:

text.NARRATIVE: Young Prompto sits down on the steps

text.Prompto: that, one day, they'd find out who I really was, and they wouldn't want me anymore.

text.NARRATIVE: Young Prompto looks up as this vision fills with memories of Prompto's journey with Noct, Gladio and Ignis, culminating in his memory of Noctis attacking him atop the train from which he fell; after a fade to white, Prompto awakens laying face down on the floor in a research lab; he grunts, looks around him, and slowly gets up onto one knee; he also now realizes the bracelet he wore to hide the barcode on the back of his right wrist is missing

text.Prompto: It's gone.

text.NARRATIVE: He stands

text.Prompto: What... What is this place?

CHOICE.SYSTEM: Construction finished today on the First Magitek Production Facility. Rising military star and leading authority on magitek Verstael Besithia has been selected to oversee the plant's operation. Reports say Besithia will relinquish his field duties in order to serve at the compound full-time.

CHOICE.Verstael: Year 722, Day 189. I received a proposal regarding a way to improve the infantry's performance by leaps and bounds: outfit the troopers with magitek cores. Preliminary tests suggest sublimating daemons for fuel will result in an unstable infantry unfit for the field. If the calculations

CHOICE.SYSTEM: provided are correct, though, this could solve all our problems. The Deathless Project marks the advent of a new age. No longer will our soldiers fall on the field of battle. The empire shall rise, and soon, all the world shall bask in our glory!

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto lays his right hand on the panel; a feminine automated voice begins speaking

text.Announcement: Scanning production code.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto gasps and looks around him; he takes a step back as the automated voice continues

text.Announcement: Unit 05953234 confirmed.

text.NARRATIVE: The metal doors before him slide open; Prompto looks down at his barcode; the voice speaks once more

text.Announcement: Warning: this unit has been compromised. Initiating retrieval of compromised unit.

text.Prompto: What's going on?

text.NARRATIVE: Suddenly, Ardyn's voice mockingly chimes in from behind Prompto

text.Ardyn: She still remembers you, after all these years.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto turns to face him

text.Prompto: You...

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto tries to conjure his weapon, but nothing appears; he looks down at his hand

text.Prompto: What gives?

text.NARRATIVE: As Ardyn walks toward Prompto, he pulls out the confused younger man's gun and waves it aloft

text.Ardyn: We can't have you spilling blood here.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto takes a step back

text.Ardyn: Although to most this compound is known only as the First Magitek Production Facility, birthplace of the myriad magitek troopers and daemons the empire holds dear, toyou this place should have some sentimental value. After all, it is your home sweet home.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto's expression becomes intense

text.Prompto: Shut up.

text.Ardyn: I'm not the one who almost killed you.

text.Prompto: You're wro—

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn suddenly lets Prompto's gun turn upside down over his finger, and shoves its handle against Prompto's chest; Prompto reaches up to grab it and Ardyn releases it into Prompto's hand; Ardyn then takes a step back

text.Ardyn: You really ought to take a rest.

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn continues taking steps back

text.Ardyn: Perhaps the estimable Chief Besithia will help heal that broken heart of yours.

text.Prompto: ... Who the hell is that?

text.Ardyn: Oh, how quickly they forget. But fear not: I've no doubt a reunion would refresh your memory.

text.NARRATIVE: Ardyn turns and begins walking away; Prompto raises his gun and points it after Ardyn, but he's already vanished; Prompto lowers and holsters the gun

text.Prompto: I'm gonna find 'em—wherever they are.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto leaves the room
After rounding the corner of the hallway outside the room, Prompto spots a magitek trooper at the other end of another hallway; a message appears

text.SYSTEM: Imperial soldiers are patrolling the area.
Equip the handgun with [up directional button], then shoot at them with R1.
The handgun will never run out of ammo, so fire away!
Strategy
Land 3 shots with a handgun.

text.NARRATIVE: After Prompto has landed the three shots, then disposed of the soldier, another message appears

text.SYSTEM: Switch from ranged to melee attacks with [left directional button].

text.NARRATIVE: Upon proceeding through the sliding doors at the end of this hall into a shorter one, Prompto finds windows to his left overlooking a large, open room filled with many dormant magitek troopers

text.Prompto: Shit... Was he telling the truth about this place?

CHOICE.Verstael: Year 722, Day 294. I acted on the proposal mentioned in my log of Day 189. My attempts to infuse the troopers' magitek cores with daemonic energy proved successful. Only in the most basic sense, however. While the soldiers are indeed deathless, they are far from fit for fighting. Thus, I've decided to take a different approach: rather than relying on daemons to power the magitek infantry, why not use humans instead? Frankly, I had never considered employing my fellow man in any magitek related experiments. But countless men and women succumb to the plasmodia each day. Rather than let them die victims of an ignominious disease, why not help them ascend to nobler heights? I've lost many a comrade on the field of battle, and I've no intention of allowing any more of their deaths to go in vain.

CHOICE.Prompto: How could he even think of using those innocent people for his twisted experiments?

text.NARRATIVE: Proceeding into an even shorter hallway, Prompto spots another magitek trooper at the end

text.Prompto: I can't let them find me.

text.SYSTEM: Approach an enemy undetected to deliver a stealth-kill.

Land a stealth-kill.

CHOICE.Verstael: Year 722, Day 339. Another day, another mental breakdown. All my tests so far have resulted in the former soldiers suffering ego deaths. Today, however, I developed a new hypothesis: I will continue to sublimate daemonified humans to harvest the miasma, but, if a sense of self is the source of these snags, why not inject

CHOICE.SYSTEM: with the plasmodia instead? We've little time. If we are to combat the Lucian threat, we must explore new options. I, too, will set aside my personal misgivings and do what I must for the empire.

CHOICE.Verstael: Year 723, Day 70. I pondered how I might find the necessary number of infants, and then it dawned on me: why not make them myself? If I clone them from my own genes, I can eliminate the pesky process of breeding them. Mass production remains a pipe dream for now, but I'm confident I can creative a massive infantry once the process picks up. If everything goes according to plan, the empire will boast a million-man army in no time at all.

CHOICE.Prompto: All this time, those things I've been fighting have been...

CHOICE.Verstael: Year 736, Day 123. It seems my laboratory is not nearly as secure as I once believed. Some thief―likely a Lucian―made off with one of my experiments. Absconding with a single infant will do nothing to enlighten them of the grandeur of my research. That said, I will see to it such an incident never arises again. I've posted magitek troopers around the facility and instructed them to keep a vigilant watch. It is their home, after all.

CHOICE.Prompto: The kingdom kidnapped one of those infants? Does that mean, I... ? No, it couldn't be. There's no way.

text.Prompto: Deep breaths...

text.Ardyn: Precisely. I thought you might like to see the fine young man he's become these twenty odd years later. So, as thanks for bringing your pets to Insomnia, I've brought the boy to you.

text.Ardyn: The time has come to meet your maker. Any questions for daddy dearest? Father and son! Oh, how I love bringing families together.

text.Prompto: No... It's not true. You're wrong, dammit!

text.Prompto: I don't care what he says. This place willnever be my home. My "home" is in Lucis—not here.

CHOICE.Verstael: Year 756, Day 98. Finally, my daemon-infused magitek armor is complete. I have christened my creation "Diamond Weapon." It has exhibited an extremely unstable psyche, immediately unleashing unmitigated horrors upon activation. Its destructive capabilities, however, are indeed beyond compare. Not even the "impenetrable" Insomnia could withstand its onslaught. Why, the Crown City would fall in a mere matter of minutes. The Stone of legend will soon be mine. To think that, in less than a month's time, the Crystal will be mine to play with as I please!

CHOICE.Prompto: So he's the one behind the attack on Insomnia... He planned the whole thing. Everything we lost that day is gone because of him.

CHOICE.SYSTEM: It is with great pride I inform Your Radiance that development has finished on the new daemon armor, Codename- Diamond Weapon. I encourage Your Radiance to visit the First Production Facility at Your Radiance's earliest convenience. I am most confident the final product will prove to Your Radiance's liking.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto enters the room where he saw Ardyn and Verstael with his weapon raised; only Verstael is here now, his back turned away from Prompto

text.Verstael: What's the matter? Have you never seen a man turn before?

text.Aranea: This one's got a ghost in the machine: Chief Besithia himself. Managed to fuse his soul with the core.

text.NARRATIVE: At the bottom of the corridor, they find an elevator, which they enter

text.Aranea: The daemons this guy created destroyed Insomnia. If we don't take him out now... ... he's liable to destroy the whole world.

text.NARRATIVE: The lift takes them further underground; they exit from it into a room with red lighting

CHOICE.SYSTEM: It has come to my attention that the Glacian's recent assault was quelled by your magitek infantry. As commendation for your service to our great nation, I have approved your petition to increase funding for your research.
Your work is the centrifugal force that will propel the empire beyond our borders to greatness on the world stage. I eagerly await further reports of your progress.
I've been assigned to Chief Besithia's lab!
Not many people can say they've worked under the
supervision of a living legend. I mean, this
the guy who saved the empire from eternal winter.
My boss pulled me aside today to issue me
and that I'm the only one qualified for the job.
But how? I barely even know my way around the
compound. Well, whatever this "task" is, I'll
deal with it in the morning.
I found out what my "special task" is
today—and frankly I wish I hadn't. If only I
could unsee the things I saw today... I really
ought eat something before I go to bed, but
that shit totally killed my appetite.
I had the honor of seeing His Imperial Majesty
in person today. To think His Radiance would travel
all that way through the ice and snow just to observe
our progress... If the emperor is putting all his
faith in magitek, then so should I!
Just my luck. One of the plasmodium samples
started leaking, and yours truly was the one
blessed with the "privilege" of cleaning it up.
And then my boss had the nerve to yell at me—as if
the whole thing were my fault! If he wants to criticize
the real culprit, he oughta look in a mirror!

text.NARRATIVE: As Aranea and Prompto enter the hallway leading out of this room, they hear an eerie sound somewhat like a mechanical howl

text.Prompto: What was that sound?

text.Aranea: Our cue to go.

CHOICE.Verstael: Year 745, Day 325. Today marks a momentous triumph for our great nation. The Glacian herself graced us with her presence in the Ghorovas Rift, and, through the combined efforts of the magitek infantry and my precious daemons, we killed her. The resulting casualties were great, but these sacrifices afforded us something far more valuable than a few units. With the data I collected, I intend to begin developing a new magitek weapon codenamed "Godslayer." Soon, all the Astrals shall bow before me and the might of my magitek. Soon, they shall know my wrath.

CHOICE.Prompto: What the hell is wrong with this guy?

CHOICE.SYSTEM: As Deputy High Commander, I hereby propose a large-scale assault on the Lucian capital of Insomnia. Preparations are to begin next month.
Our future is far too precious to entrust to our enemy. We must retrieve the Crystal and Ring of legend; only then shall our world know true peace.
Deputy High Commander Ravus Nox Fleuret

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto and Aranea enter a large open room

text.Announcement: Target detected. Eliminate immediately. Commence elimination of compromised unit.

text.NARRATIVE: The two Niflheimer heroes wipe out numerous magitek troopers and an MA Hoplomachus magitek armor

CHOICE.Aranea: Hey, you're not so worthless.
Not half bad.
You're a natural.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto and his dragoon companion enter the facility's final set of halls

CHOICE.Verstael: Year 724, Day 297. Mass production of the magitek infantry was a success. We've overwhelmed the Lucians with our numbers and surrounded Insomnia. But to rest on our laurels now would be unthinkable. On occasion, harvesting the plasmodic miasma produces some "side effects." The daemons born of this process have been disposed of on sight—until now. How foolish I was to let these sublime creatures go to waste! What they lack in adaptability, they make up for in sheer power. I realize now that I ought to channel my efforts into exploring the true potential of these daemons for the sake of the empire. Perhaps this has been my true calling all along.

CHOICE.Prompto: He's mad. This guy has completely lost his mind.

text.NARRATIVE: Descending a short set of stairs, Prompto and Aranea enter into a short hallway illuminated by red light; it is the final hallway of their journey; they hear a loud roar

text.Prompto: It must be close.

CHOICE.SYSTEM: After several years of experimentation, we have finally succeeded in fusing mammal and magitek. Although we are still conducting various tests on Codename- Barbarus, the unit should be functional enough to fend off would-be intruders until development finishes on Unit XDA-1002: Immortalis.

CHOICE.Verstael: Year 756, Day 190. At long last, my life's work is complete. Not only have I found a way to preserve the ego, I've also managed to sustain that consciousness through the sublimation process and transfer it into my magitek troopers. The prototype has proven slightly less powerful than the Diamond Weapon, but this presents no real problem. After all, one's consciousness can be transmuted again and again and again. All that remains is to fully surrender myself to my research and become my own final test subject. I will conclude my mortal life by offering a word of thanks. Chancellor Ardyn Izunia, your assistance has proved invaluable. You have my eternal gratitude. It is through your aid that I have completed my work and begun my ascension to an existence beyond divinity.

CHOICE.Prompto: Of course it was Ardyn... Everywhere we go, his name just keeps coming up. Everything that's happened to us, it's all his fault.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto and Aranea enter one more room; here, they are greeted by a large half-mammal, half-magitek creature, the Unit SAS-0822: Barbarus spoken of in the final document found in the hallway outside this room; the remains of dead magitek troopers litter the room; the fusion of mammal and magitek immediately attacks the intruders

text.Prompto: Bring it on!

text.NARRATIVE: Aranea and Prompto manage to kill the creature; once they have, they stand a few feet from its crackling remains; Prompto is gasping to catch his breath while Aranea is composed

text.Prompto: Made it out alive.

text.NARRATIVE: The room suddenly begins to shake

text.Prompto: What's going on?

text.NARRATIVE: The facility's automated voice speaks one more time

text.Announcement: Unit XDA-1002: Immortalis. Plasmodic miasma transfer complete. No psychic obstructions detected. All systems operational. Activating Immortalis.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto has a realization

text.Prompto: It's outside!

text.NARRATIVE: He and Aranea run back to the surface; once there, they see what Verstael's "life's work" has amounted to: an enormous magitek-powered worm; in place of a head, it features an enormous cannon with seven rotating components resembling drill bits spinning around the core

text.Prompto: It's gigantic...

text.NARRATIVE: Aranea runs off out of sight to acquire something

text.Prompto: So that's the "new model"... And that means... he must be inside that thing.

text.NARRATIVE: Aranea pulls up beside Prompto on another snowmobile, this one with a large machine gun mounted on the back

text.Aranea: Hop on!

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto hops on as Aranea drives them away from the research facility with the Godslayer in hot pursuit

text.Aranea: Ready for round two?

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto grabs hold of the gun's firing mechanism

text.Prompto: You bet!

text.NARRATIVE: Verstael speaks from within Immortalis as he pursues his "son" and Aranea

text.Verstael: Long have I waited to smite the world that denied me the glory I rightly deserve—and now, all shall tremble before me, man and maker alike!

text.NARRATIVE: A message appears

text.SYSTEM: Use the machine gun to take down Unit XDA-1002: Immortalis.
If Prompto is overtaken, the game will be over.
Tilt [left analog stick] or [right analog stick] to take aim.
Hold L1 or L2 to zoom in and out.
Press R1 or R2 to fire.

text.Prompto: If that's really him...

text.Aranea: That maniac's taken "biological warfare" to the next level.

text.Prompto: ... then I want to be the one to take him down.

text.NARRATIVE: The Godslayer rises from hiding under the ground at one point during its pursuit

text.Aranea: Down below!

text.Prompto: It's enormous!

text.NARRATIVE: Verstael maintains his pursuit

text.Verstael: Fall to your knees before me!

text.NARRATIVE: Under Prompto's unrelenting barrage, a component around the head of Immortalis explodes; soon after, the worm burrows underground

text.Aranea: It ain't over.

text.NARRATIVE: The Godslayer emerges from the snow once more

text.Aranea: Three o'clock!

text.NARRATIVE: Energy begins building at the tips of the mighty worm's drill-like components

text.Aranea: Incoming—look out!

text.NARRATIVE: The machine begins firing energy at Prompto and Aranea; Prompto targets these components and begins dismantling them

text.Aranea: Sharp shooting, kid. Keep it up!

text.NARRATIVE: After Prompto has disabled all but the last of the Immortalis's drill-like components

text.Prompto: This ends now.

text.NARRATIVE: When Prompto delivers what appears to be the finishing blow to the last drill-like component, there's a violent explosion and the Godslayer lifts high into the air before crumpling across the snowy landscape in a mangled heap; as it lay in the snow, seemingly burnt out, the core of the worm's head begins to glow red from within; the drill-like components become illuminated as well; Verstael's voice drips out of the machine as Immortalis rises and takes up the pursuit once more

text.Verstael: How can this be? I will not allow it!

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto continues firing away at the Godslayer as it begins charging enormous energy to fire at he and Aranea; when half of the machine's remaining life has been depleted, it looms over the snowmobile carrying Verstael's "failure" with its cannon nearly fully charged

text.Prompto: This is it!

text.NARRATIVE: When the killing blow lands, explosions rock the Godslayer, and Verstael roars as his creation comes crashing to the ground in shambles; Aranea speeds herself and Prompto away from the machine's ruin; some time later, Prompto and Aranea stand in the snow looking out over the remains of the magitek colossus Verstael had fancied capable of challenging the gods

text.Aranea: You alright?

text.Prompto: Yeah. This is what I wanted.

text.Aranea: Then say it like you mean it. You did good, kid.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto takes up a whimsical pose, and with an equally whimsical voice points at Aranea while saying his next line

text.Prompto: Couldn't have done it withoutyou, gurl!

text.NARRATIVE: He takes back up a normal stance and sober voice

text.Prompto: ... Seriously, though. Well, I'd better catch up with Noct and the guys. He's got a lot on his plate, and I figure he could probably use a hand taking back the Crystal and all that. And who knows? MaybeI'll take it back before he does!

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto runs over to the snowmobile and leans down on it; Aranea walks over to him

text.Aranea: Don't get ahead of yourself.

text.Prompto: Honestly, I don't know for sure if they're going to accept me for who I really am. But I'll never know if I don't speak up, so I'm gonna tell 'em.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto stands and turns back to Aranea

text.Prompto: After all, it's my life to live.

text.Aranea: The boy has become a man. Anyway, Gralea's straight ahead.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto gets on the snowmobile and prepares to leave; he stops

text.Prompto: Aranea!

text.NARRATIVE: She smiles at him

text.Aranea: Yeah?

text.NARRATIVE: He smiles back

text.Prompto: Thanks!

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto speeds away; Aranea watches him as he goes; unbeknownst to him, from a nearby cliff, the imperial chancellor is also watching; Ardyn mimics Prompto vocalizing the Final Fantasy victory theme and grins; the scene fades to black; against this black screen, the sound of cell doors clanging shut can be heard; the scene eventually transitions to Prompto awakening in his cell in Zegnautus Keep, struggling vainly to pull his hands free of his manacles, and then giving up; the scene fades to black once more, then fades in again to show Prompto hanging unconscious from the contraption in his cell in the background of the frame while implements of torture occupy the foreground; the scene fades to black again, then fades in once more to Prompto awakening as he is rescued from his cell by Noct and the others during Chapter 13 of the main game; he awakens to see them run into his cell and begin frantically pulling at his manacles; the visuals from the scene of them freeing him in the main game are then shown; after another brief fade to black, the scene fades in to show Prompto sitting on a bed in one of the dormitories of Zegnautus Keep; Noctis approaches, hesitates, then sits down on the opposite side of the bed, leaving the two facing away from one another

text.Prompto: For what?

text.Noctis: For falling right into his trap... and for hurting you like that.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto takes up a wry tone

text.Prompto: I know, right? How could you possibly do such a horrible thing—after everything we've been through!?

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto returns to a normal tone

text.Prompto: Nah, it's okay. You're not the only one who fell for it.

text.Noctis: Once this is all over, I say we break down the borders—come together as one nation.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto turns to look at Noct; the young king crosses his arms and tries to seem nonchalant

text.Noctis: I mean, what does it matter where you're from anyway?

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto stands and turns to look at Noctis

text.Prompto: Y'know, I never thought I'd say this, but you sounded like a real king for a second.

text.NARRATIVE: Noct appears surprised by the comment and turns to look at his friend; Prompto grins

text.Noctis: Better late than never. I'm gonna make this world a better place. You with me?

text.NARRATIVE: Noct smiles

text.Prompto: Uh-huh. Ever at your side.

text.NARRATIVE: Prompto smiles as well

text.SYSTEM: In Lestallum, a tale is told: a story about the looming shadow of oppression, and a hero who rose in resistance. Though no historical account exists, the legend nevertheless survives, telling of a nameless hero known as "the Assassin."
– Assassin's Creed

Noctis takes the Leap of Faith from atop the tower into a hay wagon below; Prompto approaches the wagon as Noctis gets out

text.Prompto: Well? Did you see him?

text.Gladiolus: We should've asked Iggy for a plan!
We shouldn't have sent him with her.

text.Ignis: Have a little faith.

text.Noctis: It may take him a while, but he always comes through in the end.

text.NARRATIVE: Feeling assured of his victory, Loqi declares as much

text.Loqi: Today, I will have my revenge!

text.NARRATIVE: At the same instant, however, the static in the air intensifies briefly, then disappears
Noctis's attacks begin damaging Loqi's magitek armor

text.Loqi: The jamming device went offline! But how?

text.Noctis: Maybe the Assassins decided to mess with you. Now it's my turn.

text.NARRATIVE: Noctis continues tearing into Loqi's magitek armor until it is wrecked

text.Loqi: If I am fated to die here, then I'll take you with me! Glory be to the Niflheim Empire!

text.NARRATIVE: Loqi's magitek armor explodes, seemingly finally killing him; the scene fades to black
The scene fades in on fireworks going off in the night sky over Lestallum; the Chocobros, Holly and Cindy are gathered in the parking area

text.Cindy: Thanks, boys. You really saved the day!

text.Noctis: Least we could do after getting you involved in all this. You're the real hero. We couldn't have done it without you.

text.Cindy: Shucks, it was nothin'. I'm just glad Holly made it back right as rain.

text.Gladiolus: Word on the street is the Assassins are the ones who sent the empire packing.

text.Ignis: That "word" should save us a world of hassle.

text.Prompto: I can see the headlines: "The Assassins are out there!" Man, at this point, even I want to believe.

text.Noctis: Why believe anything if nothing is real? And why not chase every desire you have if everything is allowed? As we say in the Brotherhood, "Nothing is true; everything is permitted."

text.Prompto: "We"? I think all that cosplay has gone to your head.

text.NARRATIVE: They all look up at the fireworks, which now include a design in the shape of the "Assasin's Creed" logo

text.Noctis: Maybe so. But my time as an Assassin taught me to take pride in doing good deeds—even if they go unseen.

text.NARRATIVE: The camera then transitions to a cloaked figure standing atop a cable car platform high above the city; the figure dives over the edge and vanishes as an eagle flies by and releases a screech; fade to black
Following the credits, two notifications then appear

text.SYSTEM: Congratulations—you have saved the Assassin's Festival!
Enjoy the festivities, and watch out for imperial soldiers.
As a token of her thanks, Holly has given you a set of Medjay Assassin's Robes.
Speak to her to change into them for the festival, or wear them in the main game.

text.NARRATIVE: The screen fades from black to Noctis and Prompto back in the parking area; a series of notifications now appear

text.SYSTEM: A new reward is available at the prize counter.
The chocobo racetrack is now open.
The Assassin's treasure hunt has begun.
Thanks for playing, and enjoy the Assassin's Festival!

CHOICE.SYSTEM: The empire has been run out of Lestallum, and the festival-goers are finally free to have fun without fear of an imperial assault. Don your Assassin's robes and enjoy the festivities!

CHOICE.Holly: I can't thank you enough, Mister Hunter.

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: The same prompt and options as before appear

CHOICE.Holly: Hope you enjoy the festival!

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: The same prompt and options as before appear

CHOICE.Cindy: Now we ain't got nothin' to worry 'bout but havin' fun!

CHOICE.Noctis: Did you get a good shot!?

CHOICE.Prompto: Uh, nope.

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: Noct groans in frustration

CHOICE.Noctis: So, you gonna take that walk or what?

CHOICE.Ignis: As it were... I already did.
Didn't want to distract with my sideshow-of-sorts. My apologies.
It would appear the key is finding your center of balance.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: What're you doing here?

CHOICE.Woman: Who's Mr. Tall-Dark-and-Handsome?

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Him? Just a buddy of mine.

CHOICE.Woman: Hunks of a feather really do flock together.

CHOICE.Noctis: What did I get myself into?

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Can't you see I'm busy here?

CHOICE.Prompto: I could never be like him.
Now he's flirting with another girl!

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: Gladio continues speaking to the woman without giving any acknowledgement to Prompto and Noctis

CHOICE.Gladiolus: I asked some guy for directions, but I ended up getting turned right back around. Sorry for the trouble.

CHOICE.Woman: No trouble at all! This place is like a maze.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Well, I may have lost my way, but I found something even better: you.

CHOICE.Woman: Aren't you the smooth talker! I bet you use that line on all the girls.

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Only the pretty ones.

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: The woman sighs with an air of delight in her voice

CHOICE.Gladiolus: Yeah, you kids run along and play.
CHOICE._Subtitle: You kids run along and play.

CHOICE.Prompto: I am disgusted.
You should offer that as a tribute to Our Goddess.

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: A prompt appears asking "Who will you give it to?"; the player can select either "Prompto" or "Cindy"

CHOICE.Prompto: You sure about this, Noct?

CHOICE.Noctis: Why shouldn't I be? She's your "goddess" after all. Give it to her and ask her for a picture.

CHOICE.Prompto: Well, I mean, if you're absolutely sure—

CHOICE.Noctis: I am. So get on with it, will you?

CHOICE.Prompto: Okay. Thanks so much, Noct. I owe you one! It's gonna be my greatest picture yet. You'll see!

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: The screen briefly fades to black; as it fades back in, Prompto is walking up to Noctis, having returned from seeing Cindy; Noct chuckles

CHOICE.Noctis: I guess that means things went well.

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: The player looks at the picture

CHOICE.Noctis: Right. It's no use in our hands anyway.

CHOICE.Prompto: I can't wait to see her smiling face!

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: A prompt appears asking "What will you do?"; the player can select either "Give her a present" or "Make conversation"

CHOICE.Noctis: Hey. I found this earlier. I don't know if you need one, but if you want it, it's yours.

CHOICE.Cindy: A gift? For me? These are mighty hard to come by, y'know. I was startin' to think they were the stuff of legends. I'd be glad to take it off your hands, but is there anything I can do to repay you?

CHOICE.Noctis: Well, if you insist, I'll trade it for a photo with you.

CHOICE.Cindy: I'd hardly call that a trade, but you got yourself a deal.

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: The screen fades to black and Prompto's deflated voice can then be heard as he prepares to take the picture

CHOICE.Prompto: Say "cheese"...

CHOICE.NARRATIVE: The camera shutter clicks; after the player examines the picture, the scene fades back in near the photo stand-in

CHOICE.Prompto: Where can we get some more of those wrenches?
CHOICE._Subtitle: No fair. I wanted to take a picture with Cindy, too. Where can we get more of those wrenches?

CHOICE.Noctis: Don't need a wrench to ask her for a picture.

CHOICE.Prompto: If only it were that easy, Noct...

text.Ignis: MTs.

text.Prompto: Why do you call 'em that?

text.Noctis: Gas stations are the same wherever you go.

text.Gladiolus: That one looks more like the gas station that time forgot.

text.Ignis: Would look a tad out of place in the crown city.

text.Prompto: Gotta love that smell though, right?

text.NARRATIVE: Note: This exchange also appears in "Final Fantasy XV: Pocket Edition," with Ignis's line rendered as "Would look a tad out of place in the Crown City."

text.Gladiolus: Let's go grab something that sticks to your ribs.

text.Ignis: "Nutrition," gentlemen. His Highness could certainly do with some green in his diet.

text.Prompto: First let's see if we can score some spicy food.

text.Gladiolus: Ooooooh.

text.NARRATIVE: Note: The audio here makes clear that this is a painful grunt

text.Gladiolus: You'll know how it feels in five years.

text.Ignis: I could do with a bath.

text.Gladiolus: Well, about time we found a place to hole up.

text.Prompto: Oh yeah, we better. Wouldn't want Ignis to feel "unkempt."

text.Ignis: You take pride in your poor hygiene?

text.Prompto: Whole lotta land out there.

text.Noctis: Bet we could cover it quicker with some chocobos.

text.Prompto: It would sure beat the hell out of walking.

text.NARRATIVE: Note: This exchange also appears in "Final Fantasy XV: Pocket Edition"

text.Gladiolus: No doubt about it: "chunky" is the only way to go.
Amazing how free we are out here.

text.Prompto: Yep
Far cry from life back home.

text.Gladiolus: Whoa, look up! Check it out.

text.Prompto: Yeah
Ever see so many stars?

text.Ignis: Not over the crown city, to be sure.

text.Prompto: Hmm
Real quiet out here, far removed from the hustle and bustle of the crown city.

text.Noctis: That's what makes it hard to stay awake.

text.NARRATIVE: Note: This exchange also appears in "Final Fantasy XV: Pocket Edition," with Prompto's line rendered as "Hm, real quiet out here. Far removed from the hustle and bustle of the Crown City."

text.Prompto: Couldn't sleep at all last night, but then I had the weirdest dream.

text.Noctis: Never knew you to be a dreamer.

text.Prompto: Always wake up before I can remember anything.

text.Noctis: What I wouldn't give for that.

text.Prompto: You are a pretty deep sleeper... like under the ground deep.

text.NARRATIVE: Note: This exchange also appears in "Final Fantasy XV: Pocket Edition," with Prompto's second line rendered as "You are a pretty deep sleeper... like under-the-ground deep."

text.Noctis: I remember thinking afternoons were the worst.

text.Prompto: That's life in the crown city, waiting for the night to set you free.
You reckon Cindy's taken?

text.Gladiolus: Don't think so.
Not exactly hard to tell. A guard like hers doesn't come down easily.

text.Prompto: Even to a Casanova like you?

text.Gladiolus: Curious as I am to see, my priority's keeping His Highness safe.

text.Ignis: You look a bit out of sorts, Noct.

text.Gladiolus: You need to take better care of yourself.

text.Noctis: Thought that's what you two were for.

text.Prompto: It just occurred to me, but this is totally like King's Knight.
There's four of us, just like in the game!

text.Noctis: Well, then I gotta be afive-star character.

text.Gladiolus: Hell no. If anyone here's a "Rare," it's me.

text.Prompto: Oh, right—King's Knight! I bet my Zell tree's almost full.
Man, wouldn't it be great if money grew on trees in real life?

text.Noctis: Sure would be. Maybe there's one out there.

text.Ignis: Any plan of attack?
I'll circle around then.
Let me give the orders this time.

text.Prompto: And simple.

text.Ignis: ... Attack.

text.Gladiolus: A big weapon like that'll leave you wide open. Try another.

text.Noctis: Ever thought about taking your own advice?

text.Ignis: Let nothing stand in your way.
Always.

text.Gladiolus: UGH. Ugliest things I've ever seen.

text.Noctis: I don't wanna go anywhere near 'em.

text.Prompto: Ha! I don't even wanna look at 'em!

text.Ignis: Hmph. I feel the same about you lot.

text.Prompto: He's got a knife! Maybe it's for cooking?

text.Gladiolus: Don't bet on it.

text.Ignis: A kitchen knife... Wonder if it's a culinary battle he wants.
MTs!

text.Prompto: Time to cut and run?

text.Ignis: Gladio's hard as a rock.

text.Noctis: The hell are you talking about!?

text.Ignis: Seems Prompto's turned into a frog.

text.Prompto: Boy, am I glad to have my voice back!
Heyyy!

text.Gladiolus: Hey, I'm gonna hit the shop.

text.Prompto: Yeah, let's stock up on everything!

text.Ignis: We can make room by leaving you behind.

text.Prompto: Smell that fresh air—makes you feel alive!

text.Noctis: Yeah, don't get used to it.

text.Gladiolus: Why is everything such a big deal with you?

text.Ignis: Let him have his fun, while he's still alive.

text.Prompto: Wonder if I'll ever get the hang of all this fighting.

text.Gladiolus: Sure you will, if you live long enough.

text.Ignis: I wouldn't count on that myself.

text.NARRATIVE: Ignis makes a "Hm" sound

text.Prompto: Knock 'em dead, Noct! I'll be sure to get lots of pics!
Nah, I think I'm okay!

text.Gladiolus: Knew you weren't completely useless!

text.Ignis: Is Prompto alright?

text.Gladiolus: He's a big boy—he'll be fine.
You've come a long way, Prompto.

text.Ignis: Impressive, Noct. You've grown stronger.

text.Noctis: Must be thanks to my balanced diet.

text.Ignis: The one that excludes vegetables?

text.Prompto: Don't you feel any jitters here on the front lines, Noct?

text.Noctis: Nah, I leave the worrying to you.

text.Ignis: It's an eat-or-be-eaten world.
Then let's dig in, shall we?

text.Gladiolus: Pull it together, Prompto! Wouldn't want to make a fool of yourself with Cindy watching.

text.Prompto: C-Cindy!? Where?
Those plants seem to have legs.

text.Ignis: And they're legging it towards us.
The coeurl acquires charge from the particles in the air
text._Subtitle: The coeurl acquires charge from particles in the air. If you see it seated on its haunches, stay back.

text.Prompto: And what if we don't?

text.Ignis: You die.

text.Prompto: Me-owch! That is one ferocious feline.
Maybe it's just me, but I feel kinda bad taking those things down.

text.Ignis: You're not alone, but out in the wild it's kill-or-be-killed.

text.Noctis: And personally, I'd prefer the former.

text.Iris: You guys kick ass.

text.Prompto: You mean it?

text.Iris: Yeah! You look cool doing it too.

text.Prompto: Yeah, we get that a lot.

text.Gladiolus: Don't take it to heart.

text.Noctis: Damn, Iris—didn't know you had it in ya.

text.Iris: Never underestimate an Amicitia.

text.Prompto: You two are a couple of beasts!

text.Gladiolus: Sure are.

text.Iris: Speak for yourself.

text.Ignis: We've no one to protect the king with his shield out of commission.

text.Gladiolus: And since when is there a king worthy of my protection?

text.Ignis: Feeling alright?

text.Noctis: You can't die. You've got hungry mouths to feed.

text.Ignis: Yours, namely?

text.Prompto: Wouldn't be the same without you, Ignis.

text.Ignis: Thank you.

text.Prompto: Guuuh! Gladio! No no no! Don't even think about dying!

text.Gladiolus: You are worried about me
